### Sexuality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Sexuality")]

Nine years after Pryor's death, in 2014, the biographical book _Becoming Richard Pryor_ by Scott Saul stated that Pryor "acknowledged his [bisexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexuality "Bisexuality")"[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-76) and, in 2018, [Quincy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Jones "Quincy Jones") and Pryor's widow Jennifer Lee stated that Pryor had a sexual relationship with actor [Marlon Brando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlon_Brando "Marlon Brando"), and that Pryor was open with his friends about his bisexuality and the fact that he slept with men.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-78) Pryor's daughter Rain later disputed the claim,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-79) to which Lee stated that Rain was in denial about her father's bisexuality.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-80)

Lee later told the Hollywood entertainment television series _[TMZ on TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TMZ\_on\_TV "TMZ on TV")_ that, "it was the '70s! Drugs were still good...If you did enough cocaine, you'd fuck a radiator and send it flowers in the morning."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-Gooden2019-82)

In his autobiography _[Pryor Convictions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pryor\_Convictions "Pryor Convictions")_, Pryor talked about having a two-week relationship with Mitrasha, a [trans woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans_woman "Trans woman"), which he called "two weeks of being gay."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-83)

In his first special, _[Live & Smokin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_&\_Smokin' "Live & Smokin'")_, Pryor discusses experimenting with [homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality "Homosexuality").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-84) Pryor later said in 1977 at a gay rights show at the [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl"), "I have sucked a dick."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-85) Pryor went on to say during the Hollywood Bowl show that the incident took place in 1952 (when Pryor was 11 or 12 years old) with someone named Wilbur Harp. Pryor also admitted to engaging in [anal sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anal_sex "Anal sex") with Harp.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-G-86)

### Substance abuse

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Substance abuse")]

Some sources (including Pryor himself) say that late in the evening of June 9, 1980, Pryor poured 151-proof [rum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rum "Rum") all over himself and set himself on fire.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:4-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-88)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:2-27) Other sources (including the Los Angeles police) say that what burned him that night was an explosion that happened while he was [freebasing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_base "Free base")[cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-nytdayafter-26) While he was still burning, he ran down Parthenia Street from his Los Angeles home until he was subdued by police. He was taken to a hospital, where he was treated for second- and third-degree burns covering more than half of his body.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-89) Pryor spent six weeks in recovery at the Grossman Burn Center at [Sherman Oaks Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Oaks_Hospital "Sherman Oaks Hospital") in Los Angeles.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-90) His daughter [Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_Pryor "Rain Pryor") stated that the incident happened as a result of a bout of drug-induced [psychosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychosis "Psychosis").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-91)

Pryor's widow Jennifer Lee recalled when he began freebasing cocaine: "After two weeks of watching him getting addicted to this stuff I moved out. It was clear the drug had moved in and it had become his lover and everything. I did not exist."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:2-27)

### Health problems

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Health problems")]

In November 1977, after many years of heavy smoking and drinking, Pryor had a mild heart attack at age 36.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:4-87) He recovered and resumed performing in January the following year. In 1986, he was diagnosed with [multiple sclerosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_sclerosis "Multiple sclerosis"), which by the mid-1990s resulted in him using a mobility scooter most of the time.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-92) In 1990, Pryor had a second heart attack while in Australia.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:3-69)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-93) He underwent triple [heart bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_bypass "Heart bypass") surgery in 1991.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-94)

In late 2004, his sister said he had lost his voice as a result of his multiple sclerosis. However, on January 9, 2005, Pryor's wife, Jennifer Lee, rebutted this statement in a post on Pryor's official website, citing Richard as saying: "I'm sick of hearing this shit about me not talking ... not true ... I have good days, bad days ... but I still am a talkin' motherfucker!"[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-95)

### Animal activism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Animal activism")]

Pryor campaigned for better welfare for animals, including through involvement in a successful campaign by [People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_for_the_Ethical_Treatment_of_Animals "People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals") targeting [KFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFC "KFC"), [Burger King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_King "Burger King"), and others for sourcing meat from suppliers that PETA claimed used inhumane practices.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:6-96) Pryor also fundraised for PETA[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-97) and was a vegetarian.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-:6-96)

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Death")]

On the morning of December 10, 2005, Pryor had a third and final heart attack at his house in Los Angeles. After his wife's failed attempts to resuscitate him, he was taken to a local Westside hospital, where he was pronounced dead at 7:58 a.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone"). His widow Jennifer was quoted as saying, "At the end, there was a smile on his face."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-BBCobit-34)

His body was [cremated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cremated "Cremated"), and his ashes were given to his family.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-99) His ashes were scattered in the bay at [Hana, Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hana,_Hawaii "Hana, Hawaii"), by his widow in 2019.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-100) Forensic pathologist [Michael Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Hunter_(forensic_pathologist) "Michael Hunter (forensic pathologist)") believes Pryor's fatal heart attack was caused by [coronary artery disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_artery_disease "Coronary artery disease") that was at least partially brought about by years of tobacco smoking.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-101)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Legacy")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Richard_Pryor_Hollywood_star_2.jpg/250px-Richard_Pryor_Hollywood_star_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Richard_Pryor_Hollywood_star_2.jpg)

Pryor's star at the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame"), covered with items left by fans

[Jerry Seinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Seinfeld "Jerry Seinfeld") called Pryor "the [Picasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picasso "Picasso") of our profession"[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-102) and [Bob Newhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Newhart "Bob Newhart") heralded Pryor as "the seminal comedian of the last 50 years".[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-103)[Dave Chappelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Chappelle "Dave Chappelle") said of Pryor, "You know those, like, evolution charts of man? He was the dude walking upright. Richard was the highest evolution of comedy."[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-autogenerated1-104) This legacy can be attributed, in part, to the unusual degree of intimacy Pryor brought to bear on his comedy. As [Bill Cosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cosby "Bill Cosby") reportedly once said, "Richard Pryor drew the line between comedy and tragedy as thin as one could possibly paint it."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-105)

### Awards and honors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Awards and honors")]

Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Richard Pryor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Richard_Pryor "List of awards and nominations received by Richard Pryor")

In 1998, Pryor won the first [Mark Twain Prize for American Humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain_Prize_for_American_Humor "Mark Twain Prize for American Humor") from the [John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-107) According to former Kennedy Center President Lawrence J. Wilker, Pryor was selected as the first recipient of the Prize because:[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-108)

> as a stand-up comic, writer, and actor, he struck a chord, and a nerve, with America, forcing it to look at large social questions of race and the more tragicomic aspects of the human condition. Though uncompromising in his wit, Pryor, like [Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain "Mark Twain"), projects a generosity of spirit that unites us. They were both trenchant social critics who spoke the truth, however outrageous.

He was listed at number one on [Comedy Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Central "Comedy Central")'s list of all-time greatest stand-up comedians.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-cc-109) In 2017, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked him first on its list of the 50 best stand-up comics of all time.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-RS-110) In a 2005 British poll to find "The Comedian's Comedian", Pryor was voted the 10th-greatest comedy act ever by fellow comedians and comedy insiders.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-111)

Pryor was posthumously awarded the [Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Lifetime_Achievement_Award "Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award") in 2006.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-112)

The animal rights organization [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PETA "PETA") gives out an award in Pryor's name to people who have done outstanding work to alleviate animal suffering. Pryor was active in animal rights and was deeply concerned about the plight of elephants in circuses and zoos.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In 1999, he was awarded a Humanitarian Award by the group,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-113) and worked with them on campaigns against the treatment of birds by [KFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFC "KFC").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-114)

Artist [Preston Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_Eugene_Jackson "Preston Eugene Jackson") created a life-sized bronze statue in dedication to the beloved comedian and named it _Richard Pryor: More than Just a Comedian_. It was placed at the corner of State and Washington Streets in downtown Peoria, on May 1, 2015, close to the neighborhood in which he grew up with his mother. The unveiling was held Sunday, May 3, 2015.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-115)

In a [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") special released in May 2022, _[The Hall: Honoring the Greats of Stand-Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hall:\_Honoring\_the\_Greats\_of\_Stand-Up "The Hall: Honoring the Greats of Stand-Up"),_ Pryor was inducted into the [National Comedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Comedy_Center "National Comedy Center") in [Jamestown, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamestown,_New_York "Jamestown, New York").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-116)

### Retrospectives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Retrospectives")]

In 2002, a television documentary entitled _The Funny Life of Richard Pryor_ depicted Pryor's life and career.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-explore.bfi.org.uk-117) Broadcast in the UK as part of the [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4") series _Kings of Black Comedy_,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-oftv.co.uk-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-highbeam.com-119) it was produced, directed and narrated by [David Upshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Upshal "David Upshal")[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-explore.bfi.org.uk-117) and featured rare clips from Pryor's 1960s stand-up appearances and films such as _[Silver Streak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver\_Streak\_(film) "Silver Streak (film)")_ (1976), _[Blue Collar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Collar\_(film) "Blue Collar (film)")_ (1978), _[Richard Pryor: Live in Concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard\_Pryor:\_Live\_in\_Concert "Richard Pryor: Live in Concert")_ (1978), and _[Stir Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_Crazy\_(film) "Stir Crazy (film)")_ (1980). Contributors included [George Carlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Carlin "George Carlin"), [Dave Chappelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Chappelle "Dave Chappelle"), [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg"), [Ice-T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice-T "Ice-T"), [Paul Mooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mooney_(comedian) "Paul Mooney (comedian)"), [Joan Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Rivers "Joan Rivers"), and [Lily Tomlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Tomlin "Lily Tomlin"). The show tracked down the two cops who had rescued Pryor from his "freebasing incident", former managers, and even school friends from Pryor's home town of [Peoria, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peoria,_Illinois "Peoria, Illinois"). In the US, the show went out as part of the _Heroes of Black Comedy_ series on [Comedy Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Central "Comedy Central"), narrated by [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-120)

A television documentary, _[Richard Pryor: I Ain't Dead Yet,#*%$#@!!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard\_Pryor:\_I\_Ain't\_Dead\_Yet "Richard Pryor: I Ain't Dead Yet")_ (2003) consisted of archival footage of Pryor's performances and testimonials from fellow comedians, including [Dave Chappelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Chappelle "Dave Chappelle"), [Denis Leary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Leary "Denis Leary"), [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock"), and [Wanda Sykes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanda_Sykes "Wanda Sykes"), on Pryor's influence on comedy.

On December 19, 2005, [BET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BET "BET") aired a Pryor special, titled _[The Funniest Man Dead or Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Funniest\_Man\_Dead\_or\_Alive "The Funniest Man Dead or Alive")_. It included commentary from fellow comedians, and insight into his upbringing.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-121)

A retrospective of Pryor's film work, concentrating on the 1970s, titled _A Pryor Engagement_, opened at [Brooklyn Academy of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Academy_of_Music "Brooklyn Academy of Music") Cinemas for a two-week run in February 2013.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-NYT-122) Many prolific comedians have claimed Pryor as an influence including [George Carlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Carlin "George Carlin"), [Dave Attell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Attell "Dave Attell"), [Martin Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lawrence "Martin Lawrence"), [Dave Chappelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Chappelle "Dave Chappelle"), [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock"), [Colin Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Quinn "Colin Quinn"), [Patrice O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_O'Neal "Patrice O'Neal"), [Bill Hicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hicks "Bill Hicks"), [Jerry Seinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Seinfeld "Jerry Seinfeld"), [Jon Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stewart "Jon Stewart"), [Bill Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Burr "Bill Burr"), [Joey Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Diaz "Joey Diaz"), [Eddie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Murphy "Eddie Murphy"), [Louis C.K.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_C.K.     *   Split LP with black ventriloquist act Richard And Willie, containing previously released tracks from _Craps (After Hours)_.

*   1977: _Richard Pryor's Greatest Hits_ ([Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Records "Warner Bros. Records")) 
    *   Contains tracks from _Craps (After Hours)_, _That Nigger's Crazy_, and _... Is It Something I Said?_, plus a previously unreleased track from 1975, "Ali".

*   1982: _The Very Best of Richard Pryor_ (Laff)
*   1983: _Richard Pryor Live_ (Laff)
*   1983: _Pissed Off!_ ([Phoenix 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laff_Records "Laff Records")) 
    *   Split LP/cassette with [Flip Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_Wilson "Flip Wilson"), containing previously released tracks from Laff Records.

*   2000: _[... And It's Deep Too! The Complete Warner Bros. Recordings (1968–1992)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...And\_It's\_Deep\_Too! "...And It's Deep Too!")_ (9-CD box set) (Warner Bros./[Rhino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhino_Records "Rhino Records")) 
    *   Box set collection containing all Warner Bros. albums plus a bonus disc of previously unissued material from 1973 to 1992.

*   2002: _[The Anthology (1968–1992)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Anthology\_(1968%E2%80%931992) "The Anthology (1968–1992)")_ (2-CD set) (Warner Bros./Rhino, [2002 in music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_in_music "2002 in music")) 
    *   Highlights culled from the albums collected in the _... And It's Deep Too!_ box set.

*   2005: _[Evolution/Revolution: The Early Years (1966–1974)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution/Revolution:\_The\_Early\_Years\_(1966%E2%80%931974) "Evolution/Revolution: The Early Years (1966–1974)")_ (2-CD set) (Warner Bros./Rhino, [2005 in music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_in_music "2005 in music")) 
    *   Pryor-authorized compilation of material released on Laff, including the entire _Craps (After Hours)_ album.

*   2013: _No Pryor Restraint: Life In Concert_ (7-CD, 2-DVD box set) ([Shout! Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shout!_Factory "Shout! Factory")/Indigo) 
    *   Box set containing concert films, albums and unreleased material from 1966 to 1992.
    *   A complimentary, limited-edition promo, entitled _Live at The Comedy Store: Hollywood, CA — October, 1973_ (Shout Factory PRO-00072 (6/13), was exclusively available to customers who pre-ordered from the company's web site.

*   2013: _The Warner Bros. Albums (1974-1983)_ (7-CD box set) (Warner Bros./Rhino) 
    *   Official albums from _That Nigger's Crazy_ to _Here and Now_.

*   2025: _I Hope I'm Funny: The Warner Albums (1974-1983)_ (7-LP box set) (Rhino) 
    *   Same content as previous Warner box set, but on vinyl only.

## Preservation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Pryor&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Preservation")]

_The Richard Pryor Special?_ was preserved by the [UCLA Film & Television Archive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA_Film_&_Television_Archive "UCLA Film & Television Archive") from an original 2 inch videotape. Preservation funding was provided by the John H. Mitchell Television Preservation Endowment. The preserved special screened at the 2024 UCLA Festival of Preservation.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor#cite_note-144)

**Lester Townes** "**Bob**" **Hope** ([né](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")**Leslie Townes Hope**; May 29, 1903 – July 27, 2003) was a British-born American comedian, actor, musician, entertainer and producer with a career that spanned nearly 80 years and achievements in [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville"), network radio, television, and [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO") Tours. He appeared in [more than 70 short and feature films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_filmography "Bob Hope filmography"), starring in 54, including a series of seven _[Road to ...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_... "Road to ...")_ musical comedy films with [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby") as his partner. He reached his 100th birthday 59 days before he died in 2003.

Hope hosted the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") ceremony a record 19 times. He also appeared in many stage productions and television roles and wrote 14 books. The song "[Thanks for the Memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanks_for_the_Memory "Thanks for the Memory")" was his signature tune. He was praised for his comedic timing, specializing in one-liners and rapid-fire delivery of jokes that were often self-deprecating. Between 1941 and 1991, he made 57 tours for the [United Service Organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Service_Organizations "United Service Organizations") (USO), entertaining military personnel around the world. In 1997, Congress passed a bill that made him an honorary veteran of the Armed Forces.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Library_of_Congress-1)

Hope was born in the [Eltham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltham "Eltham") district of southeast London. He arrived in the United States with his family at the age of four, and grew up near [Cleveland, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland,_Ohio "Cleveland, Ohio"). He became a boxer in the late 1910s, but moved into show business in the early 1920s, initially as a comedian and dancer on the vaudeville circuit before acting on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre"). He began appearing on radio and in films in his 30s, starting in 1934.

## Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early years")]

Leslie Townes Hope was born on May 29, 1903, in [Eltham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltham "Eltham"), [County of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_London "County of London")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-ReferenceA-2) (now part of the [Royal Borough of Greenwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Borough_of_Greenwich "Royal Borough of Greenwich")), in a terraced house at 44 Craigton Road in [Well Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well_Hall "Well Hall"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-BobBirthPlace-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-BobBirthPlace2-4) where there is now a British Film Institute 'Centenary of British Cinema' commemorative plaque in his memory.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-BobBirthPlace3-5) He was the fifth of seven sons of William Henry Hope, a stonemason from [Weston-super-Mare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weston-super-Mare "Weston-super-Mare"), Somerset, and Welsh mother Avis (née Townes), a light opera singer from [Barry, Vale of Glamorgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry,_Vale_of_Glamorgan "Barry, Vale of Glamorgan"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-6) who later worked as a cleaner. William and Avis married in April 1891 and lived at 12 Greenwood Street in Barry before moving to [Whitehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitehall,_Bristol "Whitehall, Bristol"), Bristol, and then to [St George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George,_Bristol "St George, Bristol"), Bristol. The family emigrated to the United States aboard the [SS _Philadelphia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Philadelphia_(1888) "SS Philadelphia (1888)"), passing through [Ellis Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island "Ellis Island"), New York on March 30, 1908, before moving on to Cleveland.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMoreno200888-7)

From age 12, Hope earned pocket money by singing, dancing, and performing comedy on the street.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens20024-8) He entered numerous dancing and amateur talent contests as Lester Hope, and won a prize in 1915 for his impersonation of [Charlie Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Chaplin "Charlie Chaplin").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-loc.gov_Early_Life-9) For a time, he attended the [Boys' Industrial School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys'_Industrial_School_(Ohio)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Boys' Industrial School (Ohio) (page does not exist)") in [Lancaster, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster,_Ohio "Lancaster, Ohio"), and as an adult donated sizable sums of money to the institution.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-ohiohistorycentral-10) He had a brief career as a boxer in 1919, fighting under the name Packy East. He had three wins and one loss, and he participated in a few staged charity bouts later in life.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Boxing-Scoop.com-11) In December 1920, 17-year-old Hope and his brothers became [US citizens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_citizens "US citizens") when their British parents became [naturalised Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_nationality_law "United States nationality law").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-12) He legally changed his name from Leslie to Lester.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Congress-13) Bob attended Fairmount Junior High and then East High in Cleveland but left before graduating. [[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-14)

In 1921, while working as a [lineman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lineman_(technician) "Lineman (technician)") for a power company, Hope was assisting his brother Jim in clearing trees when a tree fell, striking his face; his injuries required reconstructive surgery, which contributed to his later distinctive appearance.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-15) In his teens, he worked as a butcher's assistant, then briefly at Cleveland's [Chandler Motor Car Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandler_Motor_Car "Chandler Motor Car") in his early 20s.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Bob_Hope_George_Byrne.jpg/330px-Bob_Hope_George_Byrne.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_George_Byrne.jpg)

Byrne & Hope inscribed photo for the [Hilton Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilton_Twins "Hilton Twins")

Hope and his girlfriend later signed up for dancing lessons, encouraged after they performed in a three-day engagement at a club. Hope then formed a partnership with Lloyd Durbin, a friend from the dancing school.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199819%E2%80%9323-16) Silent film comedian [Fatty Arbuckle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatty_Arbuckle "Fatty Arbuckle") saw them perform in 1925 and found them work with a touring troupe called Hurley's Jolly Follies. Within a year, Hope had formed an act called the "Dancemedians" with George Byrne and the [Hilton Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilton_twins "Hilton twins"), conjoined twins who performed a tap-dancing routine on the vaudeville circuit. Hope and Byrne also had an act as [Siamese twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siamese_twins "Siamese twins"); they sang and danced while wearing blackface until friends advised Hope that he was funnier by himself.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFaith2003402%E2%80%93403-17)

In 1929, Hope informally changed his first name to "Bob". In one version of the story, he named himself after racecar driver [Bob Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Burman "Bob Burman").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199844-18) In another, he said that he chose the name because he wanted a name with a "friendly 'Hiya, fellas!' sound" to it.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200215%E2%80%9316-19) In a 1942 legal document, his legal name appears as Lester Townes Hope.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-20) After five years on the vaudeville circuit, Hope was "surprised and humbled" when he failed a 1930 screen test for the [RKO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RKO "RKO")-[Pathé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Path%C3%A9 "Pathé") short-subject studio at [Culver City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culver_City,_California "Culver City, California").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199857%E2%80%9358-21)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1927–1937: Early theatre and film roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1927–1937: Early theatre and film roles")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Bob_Hope.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope.jpg)

Bob Hope

In the early days, Hope's career included appearances on stage in vaudeville shows and Broadway productions.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-PBS-22) Hope's first Broadway appearances, in 1927's _The Sidewalks of New York_ and 1928's _Ups-a-Daisy_, were minor walk-on parts.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFaith2003403-23) He returned to Broadway in 1933 to star as Huckleberry Haines in the [Jerome Kern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Kern "Jerome Kern") and [Dorothy Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Fields "Dorothy Fields") musical _[Roberta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta\_(musical) "Roberta (musical)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199871-24) Stints in the musicals _[Say When](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say\_When\_(musical) "Say When (musical)")_, the 1936 [Ziegfeld Follies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziegfeld_Follies "Ziegfeld Follies") with [Fanny Brice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Brice "Fanny Brice"), and _[Red, Hot and Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red,\_Hot\_and\_Blue "Red, Hot and Blue")_ with [Ethel Merman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethel_Merman "Ethel Merman") and [Jimmy Durante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Durante "Jimmy Durante") followed.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199873%E2%80%9375-25)

He began performing on the radio in 1934 mostly with [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") radio, and switched to television when that medium became popular in the 1950s. He started hosting regular TV specials in 1954,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998229-26) and hosted the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") 19 times from 1939 through 1977.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-27) Overlapping with this was his movie career, spanning 1934 to 1972, and his [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO") tours, which he conducted from 1941 to 1991.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998318%E2%80%93320-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002181%E2%80%93182-29)

Hope signed a contract with [Educational Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational_Pictures "Educational Pictures") of New York for six short comedies. The first was a comedy, _[Going Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Going\_Spanish "Going Spanish")_ (1934). He was not happy with it, and told newspaper columnist [Walter Winchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Winchell "Walter Winchell"), "When they catch [bank robber] [Dillinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dillinger "Dillinger"), they're going to make him sit through it twice."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaltin197225-30) Educational Pictures took umbrage at the remark and canceled Hope's contract after only the one film. He soon signed with the [Vitaphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitaphone "Vitaphone") short-subject studio in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York, making musical and comedy shorts during the day and performing in Broadway shows in the evenings.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998105,_107-31)

### 1938–1949: Hollywood contract and stardom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1938–1949: Hollywood contract and stardom")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Bob_Hope_in_The_Ghost_Breakers_trailer.JPG/250px-Bob_Hope_in_The_Ghost_Breakers_trailer.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_in_The_Ghost_Breakers_trailer.JPG)

Bob Hope in _[The Ghost Breakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ghost\_Breakers "The Ghost Breakers")_ trailer (1940)

Hope moved to [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") when [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") signed him for the 1938 film _[The Big Broadcast of 1938](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Broadcast\_of\_1938 "The Big Broadcast of 1938")_, also starring [W. C. Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._C._Fields "W. C. Fields"). The song "[Thanks for the Memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanks_for_the_Memory "Thanks for the Memory")", which later became his trademark, was introduced in the film as a duet with [Shirley Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_Ross "Shirley Ross"), accompanied by [Shep Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shep_Fields "Shep Fields") and his orchestra.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998110,_113-32) The sentimental, fluid nature of the music allowed Hope's writers—he depended heavily upon joke writers throughout his career[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTELahr1998-33)—to later create variations of the song to fit specific circumstances, such as bidding farewell to troops while on tour or mentioning the names of towns in which he was performing.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002133-34)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Bob_Hope_and_Bing_Crosby_in_Road_to_Bali.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_and_Bing_Crosby_in_Road_to_Bali.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_and_Bing_Crosby_in_Road_to_Bali.jpg)

Hope and [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby") sing and dance during the number "Chicago Style" in _[Road to Bali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Bali "Road to Bali")_ (1952)

As a film star, Hope was best known for such comedies as _[My Favorite Brunette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Favorite\_Brunette "My Favorite Brunette")_ and the highly successful "[Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_to_... "Road to ...")" movies in which he starred with [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby") and [Dorothy Lamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Lamour "Dorothy Lamour"). The series consists of seven films made between 1940 and 1962: _[Road to Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Singapore "Road to Singapore")_ (1940), _[Road to Zanzibar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Zanzibar "Road to Zanzibar")_ (1941), _[Road to Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Morocco "Road to Morocco")_ (1942), _[Road to Utopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Utopia "Road to Utopia")_ (1946), _[Road to Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Rio "Road to Rio")_ (1947), _[Road to Bali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_to\_Bali "Road to Bali")_ (1952), and _[The Road to Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Road\_to\_Hong\_Kong "The Road to Hong Kong")_ (1962). At the outset, Paramount executives were amazed at how relaxed and compatible Hope and Crosby were as a team. What the executives didn't know was that Hope and Crosby had already worked together (on the vaudeville stage in 1932), and that working so easily in the "Road" pictures was just an extension of their old stage act.

Hope had seen Lamour performing as a nightclub singer in New York,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998112-35) and invited her to work on his [United Service Organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Service_Organizations "United Service Organizations") (USO) tours of military facilities. Lamour sometimes arrived for filming prepared with her lines, only to be baffled by completely rewritten scripts or ad-libbed dialogue between Hope and Crosby.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998128-36) Hope and Lamour were lifelong friends, and she remains the actress most associated with his film career although he made movies with dozens of [leading ladies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leading_lady "Leading lady"), including [Katharine Hepburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katharine_Hepburn "Katharine Hepburn"), [Paulette Goddard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulette_Goddard "Paulette Goddard"), [Hedy Lamarr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedy_Lamarr "Hedy Lamarr"), [Lucille Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucille_Ball "Lucille Ball"), [Rosemary Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Clooney "Rosemary Clooney"), [Jane Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Russell "Jane Russell"), and [Elke Sommer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elke_Sommer "Elke Sommer").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002174%E2%80%93180-37)

Hope and Crosby teamed not only for the "Road" pictures, but for many stage, radio, and television appearances and many brief movie appearances together over the decades[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998127-38) until Crosby died in 1977. Although the two invested together in oil leases and other business ventures, worked together frequently, and lived near each other, they rarely saw each other socially.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998127,_137-39) After the release of _Road to Singapore_ (1940), Hope's screen career took off, and he had a long and successful run. After an 11-year hiatus from the "Road" genre, he and Crosby reteamed for _The Road to Hong Kong_ (1962), starring the 28-year-old [Joan Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Collins "Joan Collins") in place of Lamour, whom Crosby thought was too old for the part.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998265-40) They had planned one more movie together in 1977, _The Road to the Fountain of Youth_, but filming was postponed when Crosby was injured in a fall, and the production was canceled when he suddenly died of heart failure that October.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998287-41)

Hope starred in 54 theatrical features between 1938 and 1972,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200241-42) as well as cameos and short films. Most of his later movies failed to match the success of his 1940s efforts. He was disappointed with his appearance in _[Cancel My Reservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel\_My\_Reservation "Cancel My Reservation")_ (1972), his last starring film; critics and filmgoers panned the movie.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998285%E2%80%93286-43) Though his career as a film star effectively ended in 1972, he did make a few cameo film appearances into the 1980s.

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/bb/Colonnahope.jpg/250px-Colonnahope.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colonnahope.jpg)

[Jerry Colonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Colonna_(entertainer) "Jerry Colonna (entertainer)") and Hope, as caricatured by [Sam Berman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Berman "Sam Berman") for NBC's 1947 promotional book

Hope's [career in broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_television_appearances "Bob Hope television appearances") began on radio in 1934. His first regular series for [NBC Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_Radio "NBC Radio") was the _Woodbury Soap Hour_ in 1937, on a 26-week contract. Serving as the master of ceremonies for these _Rippling Rhythm Revue_ radio broadcasts, Hope collaborated with the big band leader [Shep Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shep_Fields "Shep Fields") during this period of transition from vaudeville to radio.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-46) A year later, _[The Pepsodent Show Starring Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pepsodent\_Show\_Starring\_Bob\_Hope "The Pepsodent Show Starring Bob Hope")_ began, and Hope signed a ten-year contract with the show's sponsor, [Lever Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lever_Brothers "Lever Brothers"). He hired eight writers and paid them out of his salary of $2,500 a week. The original staff included [Mel Shavelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Shavelson "Mel Shavelson"), [Norman Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Panama "Norman Panama"), [Jack Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Rose_(screenwriter) "Jack Rose (screenwriter)"), [Sherwood Schwartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherwood_Schwartz "Sherwood Schwartz"), and Schwartz's brother [Al](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Schwartz_(writer) "Al Schwartz (writer)"). The writing staff eventually grew to 15.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTENachman1998144-47) The show became the top radio program in the country. Regulars on the series included [Jerry Colonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Colonna_(entertainer) "Jerry Colonna (entertainer)") and [Barbara Jo Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Jo_Allen "Barbara Jo Allen") as spinster Vera Vague. Hope continued his lucrative career in radio into the 1950s, when radio's popularity began being overshadowed by the upstart television medium.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200230%E2%80%9332-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199892%E2%80%93103-49)

### 1950–1979: Television specials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1950–1979: Television specials")]

Hope did many specials for the NBC television network in the following decades, beginning in April 1950. He was one of the first people to use [cue cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cue_card "Cue card"). The shows often were sponsored by [Frigidaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frigidaire "Frigidaire") (early 1950s), [General Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors") (1955–61), [Chrysler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler "Chrysler") (1963–73), and [Texaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texaco "Texaco") (1975–85).[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200247%E2%80%9348-50) Hope's Christmas specials were popular favorites and often featured a performance of "[Silver Bells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Bells "Silver Bells")"—from his 1951 film _[The Lemon Drop Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lemon\_Drop\_Kid "The Lemon Drop Kid")_—done as a duet with an often much younger female guest star such as [Barbara Mandrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Mandrell "Barbara Mandrell"), [Olivia Newton-John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Newton-John "Olivia Newton-John"), [Barbara Eden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Eden "Barbara Eden"), and [Brooke Shields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooke_Shields "Brooke Shields"),[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002160-51) or with his wife Dolores, a former singer with whom he dueted on two specials.

On April 26, 1970, [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") released the [Raquel Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raquel_Welch "Raquel Welch") television special _[Raquel!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raquel! "Raquel!")_; in it Hope appears as a guest.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-52) Hope's 1970 Christmas special for NBC—filmed in [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam") in front of military audiences at the height of the war—is on the list of the [highest-rated broadcasts in US history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_watched_television_broadcasts_in_the_United_States#The_highest-rated_broadcasts_of_all_time "List of most watched television broadcasts in the United States"). It was seen by more than 60 percent of the US households watching television.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200248-53) Likely the most unusual of his television specials was _Joys!_, a parody of murder mystery narratives, where the audience discovers at the end of the broadcast that Johnny Carson was the villain.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-55)

Beginning in early 1950, Hope licensed rights to publish a [celebrity comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_comics "Celebrity comics") titled _[The Adventures of Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Bob\_Hope "The Adventures of Bob Hope")_ to National Periodical Publications, alias [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics"). The comic, originally featuring publicity stills of Hope on the cover, was entirely made up of fictional stories, eventually including fictitious relatives, a high school taught by movie monsters, and a superhero called [Super-Hip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super-Hip "Super-Hip").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-RetFan25-56) It was published intermittently and continued publication through issue No. 109 in 1969. Writers included [Arnold Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Drake "Arnold Drake"), and illustrators included [Bob Oksner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Oksner "Bob Oksner") and (for the last four issues) [Neal Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal_Adams "Neal Adams").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-RetFan25-56) Hope reprised his role as Huck Haines in a 1958 production of _Roberta_ at [The Muny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Muny "The Muny") Theater in [Forest Park in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Park_(St._Louis,_Missouri) "Forest Park (St. Louis, Missouri)")[St. Louis, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis,_Missouri "St. Louis, Missouri").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-The_Muny_1958-57) Additionally, Hope rescued the [Eltham Little Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bob_Hope_Theatre "The Bob Hope Theatre") in England from closure by providing funds to buy the property. He continued his interest and support, and regularly visited the facility when in London. The theater was renamed in his honor in 1982.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-bobhopetheatre_100th-58)

### 1980–1996: Later appearances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1980–1996: Later appearances")]

Hope made a guest appearance on _The Golden Girls_, season 4, episode 17 (aired February 25, 1989) called "You Gotta Have Hope" in which Rose is convinced Bob Hope is her father. In 1992, Hope made a guest appearance as himself on the animated Fox series _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_ in the episode "[Lisa the Beauty Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_the_Beauty_Queen "Lisa the Beauty Queen")" (season 4, episode 4).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Simpsons_Season_4-59) His 90th birthday television celebration in May 1993, _Bob Hope: The First 90 Years_, won an [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award") for Outstanding Variety, Music Or Comedy Special.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Emmys_1993-60) Toward the end of his career, worsening vision problems rendered him unable to read his cue cards.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998291-61) In October 1996, he announced he was ending his 60-year contract with NBC, joking that he "decided to become a free agent".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Errico_1996-62) His final television special, _Laughing with the Presidents_, was broadcast in November 1996, with host [Tony Danza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Danza "Tony Danza") helping him present a personal retrospective of [presidents of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") known to Hope, a frequent White House visitor over the years.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-scott-63) The special, though different from his usual specials, received high praise from _Variety_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-scott-63) as well as other reviews.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Seely_2005-64) Following a brief appearance at the 50th Primetime Emmy Awards in 1997, Hope made his last TV appearance in a 1997 commercial about the introduction of [Big Kmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Kmart "Big Kmart"), directed by [Penny Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Marshall "Penny Marshall").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-K-Mart_press_release_1997-65)

Hope continued an active entertainment career past his 90th birthday, concentrating on his television specials and USO tours. Although he retired from starring in feature films after _Cancel My Reservation_, he made several cameos in films and co-starred with [Don Ameche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Ameche "Don Ameche") in the television film _[A Masterpiece of Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Masterpiece\_of\_Murder "A Masterpiece of Murder")_ (1986).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Turner_Movies-66) A television special created for his 80th birthday in 1983 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center") in Washington, D.C., featured President Ronald Reagan, actress Lucille Ball, comedian-actor-writer [George Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Burns "George Burns"), and many others.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-TV.com-67) In 1985 he was presented with the Life Achievement Award at the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors"),[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Kennedy_Center-68) and in 1998 he was appointed an honorary Knight Commander of the Most Excellent [Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (KBE) by Queen [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II"). Upon accepting the appointment, Hope quipped, "I'm speechless. 70 years of ad lib material and I'm speechless."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-CBC_News-69)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

### Academy Awards host

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Academy Awards host")]

Hope was [host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Ceremonies "Master of Ceremonies") of the Academy Awards ceremony 19 times between 1940 and 1977. His supposedly feigned desire for an Oscar became part of his act.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002154-70) While introducing the 1968 telecast, he quipped, "Welcome to the Academy Awards, or, as it's known at my house, [Passover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passover "Passover")."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCaffrey200556-71) Although he was never nominated for an Oscar, the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") honored him with four honorary awards, and in 1960 presented him with the [Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Hersholt_Humanitarian_Award "Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award"), given each year as part of the Oscars ceremony.

While aboard [RMS _Queen Mary_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RMS_Queen_Mary "RMS Queen Mary") when World War II began in September 1939, Hope volunteered to perform a special show for the passengers, during which he sang "Thanks for the Memory" with rewritten lyrics.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedrich198626-72) He performed his first USO show on May 6, 1941, at [March Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_Field "March Field") in California,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002113-73) and continued to travel and entertain troops for the rest of World War II, later during the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War"), the Vietnam War, the third phase of the [Lebanon Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon_Civil_War "Lebanon Civil War"), the latter years of the [Iran–Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "Iran–Iraq War"), and the [Persian Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf_War "Persian Gulf War").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002181%E2%80%93182-29) His USO career lasted a half-century during which he headlined 57 times.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002181%E2%80%93182-29)

He had a deep respect for the men and women who served in the armed forces, and this was reflected in his willingness to go anywhere to entertain them.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-King-74) However, during the highly controversial [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"), Hope had trouble convincing some performers to join him on tour, but he was accompanied on at least one USO tour by [Ann-Margret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann-Margret "Ann-Margret"). [Anti-war sentiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opposition_to_the_U.S._involvement_in_the_Vietnam_War "Opposition to the U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War") was high, and his pro-troop stance made him a target of criticism from some quarters. Some shows were drowned out by boos; others were listened to in silence.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002251,_254,_258-75)

The tours were funded by the U.S. Department of Defense, Hope's television sponsors, and by [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"), the network that broadcast the television specials created after each tour from footage shot on location. However, the footage and shows were owned by Hope's own production company, which made them very lucrative ventures for him, as outlined by writer [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") in his 2014 biography _Hope: Entertainer of the Century_.

Hope sometimes recruited his own family members for USO travel. His wife, Dolores, sang from atop an armored vehicle during the Desert Storm tour, and granddaughter Miranda appeared alongside him on an aircraft carrier in the Indian Ocean.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-King-74) Of Hope's USO shows in World War II, novelist [John Steinbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Steinbeck "John Steinbeck"), who then was working as a war correspondent, wrote in 1943:

> When the time for recognition of service to the nation in wartime comes to be considered, Bob Hope should be high on the list. This man drives himself and is driven. It is impossible to see how he can do so much, can cover so much ground, can work so hard, and can be so effective. He works month after month at a pace that would kill most people.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteinbeck195865-76)
