### 1980–1996: Later appearances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1980–1996: Later appearances")]

Hope made a guest appearance on _The Golden Girls_, season 4, episode 17 (aired February 25, 1989) called "You Gotta Have Hope" in which Rose is convinced Bob Hope is her father. In 1992, Hope made a guest appearance as himself on the animated Fox series _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_ in the episode "[Lisa the Beauty Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_the_Beauty_Queen "Lisa the Beauty Queen")" (season 4, episode 4).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Simpsons_Season_4-59) His 90th birthday television celebration in May 1993, _Bob Hope: The First 90 Years_, won an [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award") for Outstanding Variety, Music Or Comedy Special.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Emmys_1993-60) Toward the end of his career, worsening vision problems rendered him unable to read his cue cards.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998291-61) In October 1996, he announced he was ending his 60-year contract with NBC, joking that he "decided to become a free agent".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Errico_1996-62) His final television special, _Laughing with the Presidents_, was broadcast in November 1996, with host [Tony Danza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Danza "Tony Danza") helping him present a personal retrospective of [presidents of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") known to Hope, a frequent White House visitor over the years.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-scott-63) The special, though different from his usual specials, received high praise from _Variety_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-scott-63) as well as other reviews.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Seely_2005-64) Following a brief appearance at the 50th Primetime Emmy Awards in 1997, Hope made his last TV appearance in a 1997 commercial about the introduction of [Big Kmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Kmart "Big Kmart"), directed by [Penny Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Marshall "Penny Marshall").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-K-Mart_press_release_1997-65)

Hope continued an active entertainment career past his 90th birthday, concentrating on his television specials and USO tours. Although he retired from starring in feature films after _Cancel My Reservation_, he made several cameos in films and co-starred with [Don Ameche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Ameche "Don Ameche") in the television film _[A Masterpiece of Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Masterpiece\_of\_Murder "A Masterpiece of Murder")_ (1986).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Turner_Movies-66) A television special created for his 80th birthday in 1983 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center") in Washington, D.C., featured President Ronald Reagan, actress Lucille Ball, comedian-actor-writer [George Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Burns "George Burns"), and many others.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-TV.com-67) In 1985 he was presented with the Life Achievement Award at the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors"),[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Kennedy_Center-68) and in 1998 he was appointed an honorary Knight Commander of the Most Excellent [Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (KBE) by Queen [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II"). Upon accepting the appointment, Hope quipped, "I'm speechless. 70 years of ad lib material and I'm speechless."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-CBC_News-69)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

### Academy Awards host

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Academy Awards host")]

Hope was [host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Ceremonies "Master of Ceremonies") of the Academy Awards ceremony 19 times between 1940 and 1977. His supposedly feigned desire for an Oscar became part of his act.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002154-70) While introducing the 1968 telecast, he quipped, "Welcome to the Academy Awards, or, as it's known at my house, [Passover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passover "Passover")."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCaffrey200556-71) Although he was never nominated for an Oscar, the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") honored him with four honorary awards, and in 1960 presented him with the [Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Hersholt_Humanitarian_Award "Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award"), given each year as part of the Oscars ceremony.

### USO Involvement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: USO Involvement")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/BobHopeUSO.jpg/250px-BobHopeUSO.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BobHopeUSO.jpg)

Hope at a [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO") show

See also: [USO– Honoring Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Service_Organizations#Honoring_Bob_Hope "United Service Organizations")

While aboard [RMS _Queen Mary_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RMS_Queen_Mary "RMS Queen Mary") when World War II began in September 1939, Hope volunteered to perform a special show for the passengers, during which he sang "Thanks for the Memory" with rewritten lyrics.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedrich198626-72) He performed his first USO show on May 6, 1941, at [March Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_Field "March Field") in California,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002113-73) and continued to travel and entertain troops for the rest of World War II, later during the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War"), the Vietnam War, the third phase of the [Lebanon Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon_Civil_War "Lebanon Civil War"), the latter years of the [Iran–Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "Iran–Iraq War"), and the [Persian Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf_War "Persian Gulf War").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002181%E2%80%93182-29) His USO career lasted a half-century during which he headlined 57 times.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002181%E2%80%93182-29)

He had a deep respect for the men and women who served in the armed forces, and this was reflected in his willingness to go anywhere to entertain them.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-King-74) However, during the highly controversial [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"), Hope had trouble convincing some performers to join him on tour, but he was accompanied on at least one USO tour by [Ann-Margret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann-Margret "Ann-Margret"). [Anti-war sentiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opposition_to_the_U.S._involvement_in_the_Vietnam_War "Opposition to the U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War") was high, and his pro-troop stance made him a target of criticism from some quarters. Some shows were drowned out by boos; others were listened to in silence.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002251,_254,_258-75)

The tours were funded by the U.S. Department of Defense, Hope's television sponsors, and by [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"), the network that broadcast the television specials created after each tour from footage shot on location. However, the footage and shows were owned by Hope's own production company, which made them very lucrative ventures for him, as outlined by writer [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") in his 2014 biography _Hope: Entertainer of the Century_.

Hope sometimes recruited his own family members for USO travel. His wife, Dolores, sang from atop an armored vehicle during the Desert Storm tour, and granddaughter Miranda appeared alongside him on an aircraft carrier in the Indian Ocean.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-King-74) Of Hope's USO shows in World War II, novelist [John Steinbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Steinbeck "John Steinbeck"), who then was working as a war correspondent, wrote in 1943:

> When the time for recognition of service to the nation in wartime comes to be considered, Bob Hope should be high on the list. This man drives himself and is driven. It is impossible to see how he can do so much, can cover so much ground, can work so hard, and can be so effective. He works month after month at a pace that would kill most people.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteinbeck195865-76)

Along with his best friend Bing Crosby, Hope was offered a commission in the United States Navy as lieutenant commander during World War II, but [FDR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FDR "FDR") intervened, believing it would be better for troop morale if they kept doing what they were doing by playing for _all_ branches of military service.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHope1990119-77)

For his service to his nation through the USO, he was awarded the [Sylvanus Thayer Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvanus_Thayer_Award "Sylvanus Thayer Award") by the [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") at West Point in 1968, the first entertainer to receive the award.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Thayer_award-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-79) A 1997 act of [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") signed by President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") named Hope an "Honorary Veteran". He remarked, "I've been given many awards in my lifetime, but to be numbered among the men and women I admire most is the greatest honor I have ever received."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFaith2003429-80) In an homage to Hope, comedian/TV host [Stephen Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Colbert "Stephen Colbert") carried a golf club on stage during the week of USO performances he taped for his TV show _[The Colbert Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Colbert\_Report "The Colbert Report")_ during the 2009 season.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-LA_Times_June_2009-81)

_Dear Bob...: Bob Hope's Wartime Correspondence with the G.I.s of World War II,_ written by Martha Bolton (first woman staff writer for Bob Hope) and Linda Hope (his elder daughter), is a collection of some of his letter to the troops.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-82)

### Sports car racing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Sports car racing")]

During a short stint in 1960, Hope became a part owner of the [Riverside International Raceway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_International_Raceway "Riverside International Raceway") in [Moreno Valley, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moreno_Valley,_California "Moreno Valley, California"), along with [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") co-owner Fred Levy Jr.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-83) and oil tycoon Ed Pauley for $800,000 (adjusted to $7.0 million in 2020). [Les Richter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Richter "Les Richter") was made president of the raceway.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-84)

## Influence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Influence")]

In an interview on [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR"), [Terry Gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Gross "Terry Gross") said, "[Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") and [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") are two of the people who have referred to Bob Hope as influences. And I think influences in part on their own personas as not being this suave, handsome, macho guy." Hope biographer Zoglin agreed saying, "Woody continually said, this was the guy who influenced me more than anyone else. And that character - that kind of scared character, the guy talk - nervous, talking his way through, you know, bad times and scary times. That was Woody Allen's character in _[Sleeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper\_(1973\_film) "Sleeper (1973 film)")_ (1973) and _[Love and Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_and\_Death "Love and Death")_ (1975). He always said that he and [Diane Keaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Keaton "Diane Keaton") in those films were basically like Hope and [Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby")".[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-85)

[Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") also cited Hope as an influence saying, "I loved Woody Allen. And Woody Allen says, oh, I love Bob Hope, he really influenced me. And I thought, what are you talking about? How did Bob Hope influence you in any way?...Then I went back and I started looking at seeing some of the movies. And you see it, you see that that the character that Woody Allen does is a character that I think was really, to a large extent invented by Bob Hope."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-86)

## Artistry and legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Artistry and legacy")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Cat-and-the-Canary-1939.jpg/250px-Cat-and-the-Canary-1939.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cat-and-the-Canary-1939.jpg)

[Douglass Montgomery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglass_Montgomery "Douglass Montgomery"), Bob Hope, [Paulette Goddard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulette_Goddard "Paulette Goddard") and [John Beal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Beal_(actor) "John Beal (actor)") in _[The Cat and the Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cat\_and\_the\_Canary\_(1939\_film) "The Cat and the Canary (1939 film)")_ (1939)

Hope helped establish modern American comedy.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-PBS-22) He was widely praised for his comedic timing and his specialization in the use of [one-liners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-liner_joke "One-liner joke") and rapid-fire delivery of jokes. He was known for his style of self-deprecating jokes, first building himself up and then tearing himself down. He performed hundreds of times per year.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998158-87) Such early films as _[The Cat and the Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cat\_and\_the\_Canary\_(1939\_film) "The Cat and the Canary (1939 film)")_ (1939) and _[The Paleface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Paleface\_(1948\_film) "The Paleface (1948 film)")_ (1948) were financially successful and praised by critics,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998123,_183-88) and by the mid-1940s, with his radio program getting good ratings as well, he was one of the most popular entertainers in the United States.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998153-89) When Paramount threatened to stop production of the "Road" pictures in 1945, they received 75,000 letters of protest.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998172-90)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Jerry_colonna_bob_hope_1940_nbc.JPG/250px-Jerry_colonna_bob_hope_1940_nbc.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jerry_colonna_bob_hope_1940_nbc.JPG)

Hope and his comic sidekick, [Jerry Colonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Colonna_(entertainer) "Jerry Colonna (entertainer)"), sporting his trademark handlebar mustache in 1940

Hope had no faith in his skills as a dramatic actor, and his performances of that type were not as well received.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998184,_187-91) He had been well known in radio until the late 1940s; however, as his ratings began to slip in the 1950s, he switched to television and became an early pioneer of that medium.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002160-51)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998173-92) He published several books, notably dictating to [ghostwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter") about his wartime experiences.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998153-89)

Although Hope made an effort to keep his material up to date, he never adapted his comic persona or his routines to any great degree. As Hollywood began to transition to the "[New Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hollywood "New Hollywood")" era in the 1960s, he reacted negatively, such as when he hosted the [40th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40th_Academy_Awards "40th Academy Awards") in 1968 and voiced his contempt by mocking the show's delay because of the assassination of [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr. "Martin Luther King Jr.") and condescendingly greeted attending younger actors on stage—such as [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman"), who was 30 at the time—as children.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-93) By the 1970s, his popularity was beginning to wane with military personnel and with the movie-going public in general.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998255,_276,_314-94) However, he continued doing USO tours into the 1980s[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002161-95) and continued to appear on television into the 1990s. Former First Lady [Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan"), a close friend and frequent host to him at the White House, called Hope "America's most honored citizen and our favorite clown".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998312-96)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Bob_Hope_playing_golf_in_the_Oval_Office.png/250px-Bob_Hope_playing_golf_in_the_Oval_Office.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_playing_golf_in_the_Oval_Office.png)

Hope, a golf fan, putting a golf ball into an ashtray held by President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") in the [Oval Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office") in 1973

Hope was well known as an avid golfer, playing in as many as 150 charity tournaments a year.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200257-97) Introduced to the game in the 1930s while performing in [Winnipeg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg "Winnipeg"), Canada,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Manitoba_Historic_Society_1988-98) he eventually played to a four [handicap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_handicap "Golf handicap"). His love for the game—and the humor he could find in it—made him a sought-after [foursome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foursome_(golf) "Foursome (golf)") member. He once remarked that President [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower") gave up golf for painting: "Fewer strokes, you know."[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-panews_May_1980-99) He also was quoted as saying, "It's wonderful how you can start out with three strangers in the morning, play 18 holes, and by the time the day is over you have three solid enemies."[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Golf_Hall_of_Fame-100)

A golf club became an integral [prop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prop "Prop") for Hope during the standup segments of his television specials and USO shows. In 1978 he putted against the then-two-year-old [Tiger Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Woods "Tiger Woods") in a television appearance with the actor [Jimmy Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Stewart "Jimmy Stewart") on _[The Mike Douglas Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mike\_Douglas\_Show "The Mike Douglas Show")_.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Fox_Sports_2012-101)

The [Bob Hope Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Classic "Bob Hope Classic"), founded in 1960, made history in 1995 when Hope teed up for the opening round in a foursome that included presidents [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford"), [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), and [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), the only time three U.S. presidents played in the same golf foursome.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-bhcc_History-102) The event, now known as the CareerBuilder Challenge, was one of the few [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour") tournaments that took place over five rounds, until the 2012 tournament when it was cut back to the conventional four.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Business_Wire-103)

Hope had a heavy interest in sports beyond golf and his brief fling as a professional boxer in his youth. In 1946, he bought a small stake in the [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians") professional baseball team[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Windsor_Star_1946-104) and held it for most of the rest of his life.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Rea_1982-105) He appeared on the June 3, 1963, cover of _[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ magazine wearing an Indians uniform,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Sports_Illustrated_cover-106) and sang a special version of "Thanks for the Memories" after the Indians' last game at [Cleveland Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Stadium "Cleveland Stadium") on October 3, 1993.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Dawidziak_2003-107) He also bought a share with Bing Crosby of the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") football team in 1947, but sold it in 1962.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Lodi_News_1962-108) He frequently used his television specials to promote the annual [AP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press")[College Football All-America Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_All-America_Team "College Football All-America Team"). The players would come onstage one by one and introduce themselves, then Hope, often dressed in a football uniform, would give a one-liner about the player or his school.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FWAA_2009-109)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg)

Hope and his wife Dolores on [Capitol Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Hill "Capitol Hill") as he received an award in 1978

Hope was awarded more than 2,000 honors and awards, including 54 honorary university doctorates. In 1963 President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") awarded him the [Congressional Gold Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Gold_Medal "Congressional Gold Medal") for service to his country.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002152%E2%80%93153-110) President [Lyndon Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson "Lyndon Johnson") bestowed the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom") in 1969 for his service to the armed forces through the [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-usa-patriotism.com-111) In 1982 he received the S. Roger Horchow Award for Greatest Public Service by a Private Citizen, an honor given annually by [Jefferson Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Awards "Jefferson Awards").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Horchow_Award-112) He was presented with the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 1995[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-National_Medal_of_Arts-113) and received the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award") in 1997.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Times_Union_1997-114) On June 10, 1980, he became the 64th—and only civilian—recipient of the United States Air Force [Order of the Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Sword_(United_States) "Order of the Sword (United States)") which recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to the enlisted corps.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Air_University-115)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg/250px-Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg)

[Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") prepares to present Hope (then aged 94) with the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award"), July 1997

Several buildings and facilities were renamed for Hope, including the historic [Fox California Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Theater_(Stockton,_California)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fox Theater (Stockton, California) (page does not exist)") in downtown [Stockton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockton,_California "Stockton, California"),[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Mohawk_Group-116) and the [Bob Hope Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Airport "Bob Hope Airport") in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Daily_News_2010-117) There is a Bob Hope Gallery at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-118) In memory of his mother, Avis Townes Hope, Bob and Dolores Hope gave the [Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_National_Shrine_of_the_Immaculate_Conception "Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception") in Washington, D.C., a chapel called the Chapel of [Our Lady of Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Hope "Our Lady of Hope").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-119)[USNS _Bob Hope_(T-AKR-300)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope") of the U.S. [Military Sealift Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") was named for the performer in 1997. It is one of very few [U.S. naval ships that were named after living people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._military_vessels_named_after_living_Americans "List of U.S. military vessels named after living Americans").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FAS_2011-120) The Air Force named a [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III") transport aircraft the _Spirit of Bob Hope_.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Warplanes_Online_Community-121)

In 1965, he was awarded an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters (L.H.D.) degree from [Whittier College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_College "Whittier College").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-122)

In 1978, Hope was invited to [dot the "i"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band#Script_Ohio_and_dotting_the_%22i%22 "Ohio State University Marching Band") in the [Ohio State University Marching Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band "Ohio State University Marching Band")'s "Script Ohio" formation, an honor only given to non-band members on 14 occasions from 1936 through 2016.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-123)[Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") wrote and narrated a documentary honoring him, _My Favorite Comedian_, shown at [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center "Lincoln Center").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-124) In Hope's hometown of Cleveland, the refurbished [Lorain-Carnegie Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorain-Carnegie_Bridge "Lorain-Carnegie Bridge") was renamed the Hope Memorial Bridge in 1983, though differing claims have been made as to whether the bridge honors Hope himself, his entire family, or his stonemason father who helped in the bridge's construction. Also, East 14th Street near [Playhouse Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playhouse_Square "Playhouse Square") in Cleveland's theater district was renamed Memory Lane-Bob Hope Way in 2003 in honor of the entertainer's 100th birthday.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-125)

In 1992, Hope was honored with the "Lombardi Award of Excellence" from the Vince Lombardi Cancer Foundation. The award was created to honor the football coach's legacy, and is awarded annually to an individual who exemplifies his spirit. He was also inducted into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa"), the National Leadership Honor Society, in 1992 at [Ferris State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_State_University "Ferris State University"). On May 28, 2003, President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") established the [Bob Hope American Patriot Award](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2013306 "s:Executive Order 13306").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-126)

**Academy Awards** Although he was never nominated for a competitive Oscar, Hope was given five honorary awards by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences"):[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-awardsdatabase-127)

*   [13th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_Academy_Awards "13th Academy Awards") (1940): Special Award in recognition of his unselfish services to the motion picture industry
*   [17th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17th_Academy_Awards "17th Academy Awards") (1944): Special Award for his many services to the academy
*   [25th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25th_Academy_Awards "25th Academy Awards") (1952): Honorary Award for his contribution to the laughter of the world, his service to the motion picture industry, and his devotion to the American premise
*   [32nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Academy_Awards "32nd Academy Awards") (1959): [Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Hersholt_Humanitarian_Award "Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award")
*   [38th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/38th_Academy_Awards "38th Academy Awards") (1965): Honorary Award: first Academy Gold Medal for unique and distinguished service to the industry and the academy

Hope was briefly married to vaudeville partner Grace Louise Troxell (1912–1992), a secretary from Chicago, Illinois. They were married on January 25, 1933, in Erie, Pennsylvania.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199866-128) They divorced in November 1934.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-129)

The couple had shared headliner status with Joe Howard at the Palace Theatre in April 1931, performing "Keep Smiling" and the "Antics of 1931".[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-130) They worked together at the RKO Albee, performing the "Antics of 1933" along with Ann Gillens and Johnny Peters in June of that year.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-131) The following month, singer [Dolores Reade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Reade "Dolores Reade") joined Hope's vaudeville troupe and was performing with him at Loew's Metropolitan Theater. ### Politics and beliefs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Politics and beliefs")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg/250px-Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg)

From left to right: [Spiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiro_Agnew "Spiro Agnew") and [Judy Agnew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Agnew "Judy Agnew"), Bob and [Dolores Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Hope "Dolores Hope"), [Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Pat Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon"), [Nancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") during a campaign stop for the [Nixon-Agnew ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon-Agnew_ticket "Nixon-Agnew ticket") in California, 1971

Hope had extensive relationships with US Presidents from [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") to [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and often made topical political jokes in his comedic material. He hosted the [White House Correspondents Dinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Correspondents_Dinner "White House Correspondents Dinner") three times in 1944, 1953, and 1976.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-ford-146) Hope was supportive politically of [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") Presidents such as [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-148)

In an interview with Hope biographer [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") on [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") he stated that "Bob Hope was the establishment. Bob Hope was friends with [Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon "Nixon"). Bob Hope was speaking in favor of the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"). Bob Hope was expressing that kind of backward, suburban, [WASP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WASP "WASP") view of minorities, [homosexuals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuals "Homosexuals"), the [women's movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_movement "Women's movement")."[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-149) Hope's beliefs and attitudes on social issues are a part of the plot of the 2020 film _[Misbehaviour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misbehaviour\_(film) "Misbehaviour (film)")_, which follows the [Women's Liberation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Liberation "Women's Liberation") protests at the [Miss World 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_World_1970 "Miss World 1970") competition that Hope hosted; [Greg Kinnear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kinnear "Greg Kinnear") plays Hope.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-150)

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/President_Ronald_Reagan_and_Nancy_Reagan_Talking_with_Bob_Hope_During_The_State_Dinner_for_Prime_Minister_Thatcher_at_The_White_House_-_DPLA_-_2db8a4b53ef061b70538102c33453b61.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Ronald_Reagan_and_Nancy_Reagan_Talking_with_Bob_Hope_During_The_State_Dinner_for_Prime_Minister_Thatcher_at_The_White_House_-_DPLA_-_2db8a4b53ef061b70538102c33453b61.jpg)

Hope (left) with [Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and President [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") in 1981

After the shootings of president Ronald Reagan and [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") in 1981, Hope advocated for [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control "Gun control"). Hope told [Tom Shales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shales "Tom Shales") of _The Washington Post_, "I'm for gun registration. I don't think any jerk that's coked up or anything should be allowed to walk in a store and buy a gun and turn around and shoot 19 people, you know? ... And what the hell, hunters can have their guns, they're registered. I've got a gun in each house for a warning thing; that can be registered ... They gotta tell me what's wrong with having them registered. That's all I wanna hear."[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-151) When Hope shared these views during an [ABC Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_Radio "ABC News Radio") interview, he quickly realized the repercussions. Vice President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), who was visiting [West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point "West Point") the same day Hope taped a special there, had declined to meet with him. Additionally, at a luncheon in Washington that same week, Hope had planned to sit with Nancy Reagan, but she canceled at the last minute.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-152)

Hope's views on the gay community also evolved. At the height of [Anita Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Bryant "Anita Bryant")'s campaign to reverse the progress of gay rights and anti-discrimination legislation in Florida in 1977, he, as well as many other comedians, ridiculed her in their routines, but also expressed his disagreement with Bryant: "We're all entitled to our own sexual habits [and] I believe what these people do behind closed doors is their business ... During a performance at [Liberty Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Weekend "Liberty Weekend") in 1986, Hope remarked, "I just heard that the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty") has AIDS, but she doesn't know if she got it from the mouth of the [Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River") or the [Staten Island Ferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Ferry "Staten Island Ferry")."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-156) Two months later, Hope took responsibility for telling the joke and apologized, explaining that he overheard the joke and thought it was funny.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-157) When Hope used the word "[fag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faggot "Faggot")" on a 1988 _[Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_ appearance, [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") asked for a statement apologizing for the slur. He agreed to tape a public service announcement opposing "bigotry" on their behalf.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-158)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Philanthropy and estate")]

It was put on the market in late 2012.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMikailian2012-161)

The [Hope Residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Residence "Hope Residence") is a 23,366-square-foot (2,171 m 2)[modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism "Modernism") home in [Palm Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs "Palm Springs"), built to resemble a volcano, that was designed in 1973 by [John Lautner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lautner "John Lautner"). The home is located above the city, with panoramic views of the [Coachella Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley "Coachella Valley") and the [San Jacinto Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto_Mountains "San Jacinto Mountains"). It was put on the market for the first time in February 2013 with an asking price of $50 million,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-NYTimes_February_2013-162) and sold to investor [Ron Burkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Burkle "Ron Burkle") for just $13 million in November 2016.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&search=Greek+??#cite_note-163)

## Honors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Honors")]

*   Recipient of the Golden Plate Award of the [American Academy of Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Achievement "Academy of Achievement") in 1961[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-1)

*   Recipient of the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 1985
*   Induction into the [Television Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Hall_of_Fame "Television Hall of Fame") in 1987
*   Induction into the [World Golf Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Golf_Hall_of_Fame "World Golf Hall of Fame") in 1983
*   Recipient of the [Arkansas Traveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_Traveler_(honorary_title) "Arkansas Traveler (honorary title)")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-2)
*   Induction into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa"), the National Leadership Honor Society in 1992

*   [Sylvanus Thayer Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvanus_Thayer_Award "Sylvanus Thayer Award"), [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") (at West Point, 1968)

### Titles and designations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Titles and designations")]

*   [1948 World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_World_Series "1948 World Series") Champion (as part owner of the [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians")).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-7)
*   Honorary mayor of [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California") (1950s)
*   [Hasty Pudding Man of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasty_Pudding_Man_of_the_Year "Hasty Pudding Man of the Year") (first awardee, 1967)
*   [Board of Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Governors "Board of Governors") of the [National Space Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Institute "National Space Institute"), forerunner of the present-day [National Space Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Society "National Space Society"), a [nonprofit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit "Nonprofit") educational [space advocacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_advocacy "Space advocacy") organization founded by Dr. [Wernher von Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wernher_von_Braun "Wernher von Braun") (1974)
*   _Honorary Veteran of the United States Armed Forces_, a tribute from the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") given in recognition of the entertainment he provided U.S. troops during [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War "War") and peacekeeping missions (October 29, 1997)
*   Honorary [Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (KBE) _In recognition of his contributions to film, to song, and to the entertainment of troops in the past._ (1998).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-BBC_1998-8) He had previously been appointed an Honorary Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 1976.
*   Knighthood, Order of St. Sylvester from the [Vatican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church "Roman Catholic Church")
*   [Silver Buffalo Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Buffalo_Award "Silver Buffalo Award") (highest adult award given by the [Boy Scouts of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Scouts_of_America "Boy Scouts of America"))
*   The Honorable Order of [Kentucky Colonels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Colonel "Kentucky Colonel").
*   The [Grand Order of Water Rats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Order_of_Water_Rats "Grand Order of Water Rats").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-9)
*   Appointed a Knight Commander with Star of the [Order of St. Gregory the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St._Gregory_the_Great "Order of St. Gregory the Great") by [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") in 1998[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-LA_Times_1998-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Golf_Hall_of_Fame-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-NAB_Hall_of_Fame-12)
*   Hope became the 64th and only civilian recipient of the United States Air Force [Order of the Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Sword_(United_States) "Order of the Sword (United States)") on June 10, 1980. The Order of the Sword recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to the enlisted corps.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Air_University-13)
*   In 1996 Hope was awarded the Naval Heritage Award by the [U S Navy Memorial Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Memorial "Navy Memorial") for his support of the US Navy and military.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Lone_Sailor_Award-14)

### Memorials and tributes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Memorials and tributes")]

*   The [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour")'s [Bob Hope Chrysler Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Chrysler_Classic "Bob Hope Chrysler Classic"), which was an existing tournament (The Desert Classic) renamed in recognition of the comedian's lifelong passion for the game, 1966
*   The [Lorain-Carnegie Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorain-Carnegie_Bridge "Lorain-Carnegie Bridge") in Cleveland was renamed the Hope Memorial Bridge in 1983 (disputed as to whether it was meant to honor Hope, his stonemason father Harry, or the entire Hope Family)
*   _America's Tribute to Bob Hope_, a 1988 documentary taped at the [Palm Desert, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Desert,_California "Palm Desert, California"), Bob Hope Cultural Center[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-15)
*   In 1992, a Golden Palm Star on the [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California"), [Walk of Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs_Walk_of_Stars "Palm Springs Walk of Stars") was dedicated to him.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Walk_of_Stars-16)
*   Bob Hope Drive, streets in both [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") (where there is also an airport named after him)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Daily_News_2010-17) and [Rancho Mirage, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Mirage,_California "Rancho Mirage, California"). The Rancho Mirage street is the location of [Eisenhower Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenhower_Medical_Center "Eisenhower Medical Center") which Hope and his wife were instrumental in creating.

_The Spirit of Bob Hope_ is a USAF C-17 Globemaster III that was named after Hope

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Bob_Hope_%28signature_and_handprints%29.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_%28signature_and_handprints%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_(signature_and_handprints).jpg)

The handprints of Bob Hope in front of [The Great Movie Ride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_Movie_Ride "The Great Movie Ride") at [Disney's Hollywood Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney's_Hollywood_Studios "Disney's Hollywood Studios")

*   [The United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_United_States_Air_Force "The United States Air Force") named a [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III") transport aircraft the _Spirit of Bob Hope_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Warplanes_Online_Community-18)
*   _Bob Hope: 50 Years of Hope_, an exhibition of Hope's service of entertaining the United States military at the [National Museum of the United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_the_United_States_Air_Force "National Museum of the United States Air Force") near [Dayton, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio")[](https://web.archive.org/web/20021028073736/http://www.wpafb.af.mil/museum/pa/nr021031.htm)
*   [Bob Hope Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Square "Bob Hope Square") (naming of the intersection at [Hollywood and Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_and_Vine "Hollywood and Vine") in Los Angeles to commemorate Hope's 100th birthday, May 29, 2003)
*   Memory Lane-Bob Hope Way (renaming of East 14th Street in [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") to commemorate Hope's 100th birthday in 2003)
*   Bob Hope Airport: Hope had joked with his family that he wanted an airport named for him after hearing in 1979 that [Orange County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_County,_California "Orange County, California") officials had renamed their airport after [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne"). On November 3, 2003 the [Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena_Airport "Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport") Authority voted unanimously to rename the facility and on November 18, 2003 the [Glendale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_California "Glendale, California"), and [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") city councils voted unanimously to approve it. [Pasadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California") followed on December 10. The [FAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration") three-letter designation BUR did not change. A rededication ceremony took place on December 17, the 100th anniversary of the [Wright brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_brothers "Wright brothers")' first powered flight.
*   The historic Fox Theater in downtown [Stockton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockton,_California "Stockton, California"), was renamed the Bob Hope Theater in his honor. The building is listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Mohawk_Group-19)
*   [USNS _Bob Hope_(T-AKR-300)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope") of the U.S. [Military Sealift Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") was named after the performer in 1997. It is one of very few [U.S. naval ships that were named after living people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._military_vessels_named_after_living_Americans "List of U.S. military vessels named after living Americans").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-FAS_2011-20)
*   _[Asteroid 2829 Bobhope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2829\_Bobhope "2829 Bobhope")_
*   The Bob Hope Theatre, an amateur theatre (although professional musicians receive payment) in [Eltham, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltham,_London "Eltham, London"), where he was born. He personally funded the theatre in 1980 to develop further projects for the venue.
*   [Blue plaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_plaque "Blue plaque") at 44, Craigton Road [Eltham, London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltham,_London "Eltham, London"), Hope's place of birth.
*   The Bob Hope Theatre, an on-base movie theatre and lecture hall at [Marine Corps Air Station Miramar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_Miramar "Marine Corps Air Station Miramar"), [San Diego, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego,_California "San Diego, California").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-mccsmiramar-21)
*   Hope had a long and close association with [Southern Methodist University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Methodist_University "Southern Methodist University") in [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"). His donations of over $800,000 enabled the opening of the Bob Hope Theatre in the Owen Fine Arts Center of the [Meadows School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meadows_School_of_the_Arts "Meadows School of the Arts"), and two theater scholarships and an award are named in his honor.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Southern_Methodist_University-22)
*   "The Bob Hope Chow Hall", the dining facility at [Camp Lemonnier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Lemonnier "Camp Lemonnier"), Djibouti, Africa.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-23)
*   Bob Hope Primary School, a [primary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_school "Primary school") located on Kadena US Air Force Base, in Okinawa, Japan.
*   The historic [Bob Hope Patriotic Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Patriotic_Hall "Bob Hope Patriotic Hall") building on [Figueroa Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Figueroa_Street "Figueroa Street") in [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County "Los Angeles County") was named in his honor on August 3, 2003, by the [Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Board_of_Supervisors "Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Molina_2009-24)
*   In a bill passed by Congress in 2008, the research library at the [Ellis Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island "Ellis Island") Immigration Museum was renamed the Bob Hope Memorial Library.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Chan_2008-25)
*   At the U.S. Naval Academy, [Alumni Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alumni_Hall_(Navy) "Alumni Hall (Navy)") is home to the Bob Hope Performing Arts Center.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlake2010135-26)

**Edgar John Bergen** (né **Berggren**; February 16, 1903– September 30, 1978) was an American ventriloquist, comedian, actor, vaudevillian and radio performer. He was best known for his characters [Charlie McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_McCarthy "Charlie McCarthy") and Mortimer Snerd. Bergen pioneered modern-day [ventriloquism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventriloquism "Ventriloquism") and has been described by puppetry organization [UNIMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNIMA "UNIMA") as the “quintessential ventriloquist of the 20th century”.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-1) He was the father of actress [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Edgar_Bergen_and_Charlie_McCarthy_1926.jpg/250px-Edgar_Bergen_and_Charlie_McCarthy_1926.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Edgar_Bergen_and_Charlie_McCarthy_1926.jpg)

Bergen and [Charlie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_McCarthy_(ventriloquist) "Charlie McCarthy (ventriloquist)") in 1926

Bergen was born in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), one of five children and the younger of two sons of [Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden") immigrants Nilla Svensdotter (née Osberg) and Johan Henriksson Berggren.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-2) He lived on a farm near [Decatur, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decatur,_Michigan "Decatur, Michigan") until he was four, when his family returned to Sweden, where he learned the language. After his family had returned to Chicago, when he was eleven, he taught himself ventriloquism from a pamphlet called "The Wizard's Manual". He attended [Lake View High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_View_High_School_(Chicago,_Illinois) "Lake View High School (Chicago, Illinois)"). After his father died, when Edgar was 16, he went out to work as an apprentice accountant, a furnace stoker, a player-piano operator, and a projectionist in a silent-movie house.

Edgar so impressed the famous ventriloquist [Harry Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Lester_(ventriloquist) "Harry Lester (ventriloquist)") that he gave the teenager almost daily lessons for three months in the fundamentals of ventriloquism. In the fall of 1919, Edgar paid Chicago woodcarver Theodore Mack $36 ($688.59 in 2025) to sculpt a likeness of a rascally red-headed Irish [newspaper boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper_hawker "Newspaper hawker") he knew. The head went on a [dummy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventriloquism "Ventriloquism") named Charlie McCarthy, which became Bergen's lifelong [sidekick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidekick "Sidekick"). He had created the body himself, using a nine-inch length of broomstick for the backbone, and rubber bands and cords to control the lower jaw mechanism of the mouth.

For college, he attended [Northwestern University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University "Northwestern University"), where he enrolled in the pre-med program to please his mother. He later switched to speech and drama, but never completed his degree.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-3) He gave his first public performance at Waveland Avenue Congregational Church located on the northeast corner of Waveland and Janssen. He lived across the street from the church. In 1965, he gave the church a generous contribution, a thoughtful letter, and a photograph of himself which had been requested by the minister and was displayed in the church's assembly room which was dedicated to Bergen. He cut out an "R" and a "G" from his family name and went from Berggren to Bergen on the showbills. Between June 1922 and August 1925, he performed every summer on the professional [Chautauqua circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chautauqua_circuit "Chautauqua circuit") and at the Lyceum theater in Chicago. Bergen had an interest in aviation, becoming a private pilot.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-4)

## _The Chase and Sanborn Hour_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: The Chase and Sanborn Hour")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Chase_and_Sanborn_Hour.jpg/250px-Chase_and_Sanborn_Hour.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chase_and_Sanborn_Hour.jpg)

Edgar Bergen and his dummy Charlie McCarthy with [W. C. Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._C._Fields "W. C. Fields") on _[The Chase and Sanborn Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_and\_Sanborn\_Hour "The Chase and Sanborn Hour")_

His first performances were in [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville"), at which point he legally changed his last name to the easier-to-pronounce "Bergen". He worked in one-reel [movie shorts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_subject "Short subject"), but his real success was on the radio. He and Charlie were seen at a New York party by [Elsa Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa_Maxwell "Elsa Maxwell") for [Noël Coward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No%C3%ABl_Coward "Noël Coward"), who recommended them for an engagement at the famous [Rainbow Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Room "Rainbow Room"). It was there that two producers saw Bergen and Charlie perform. They then recommended them for a guest appearance on [Rudy Vallée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Vall%C3%A9e "Rudy Vallée")'s program.

Their initial appearance (December 17, 1936) was so successful that the following year they were given regular cast roles as part of _[The Chase and Sanborn Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_and\_Sanborn\_Hour "The Chase and Sanborn Hour")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-Dunning-5) Under various sponsors (and two different networks), they were on the air from May 9, 1937, to July 1, 1956. The popularity of a ventriloquist on radio, when one could see neither the dummies nor his skill, surprised and puzzled many critics, then and now. Even knowing that Bergen provided the voice, listeners perceived Charlie as a genuine person.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-6) In 1947, Sam Berman caricatured Bergen and McCarthy for the network's glossy promotional book, _NBC Parade of Stars: As Heard Over Your Favorite NBC Station_.

Bergen's skill as an entertainer, especially his characterization of Charlie, carried the show (many recordings of which have survived).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-Dunning-5) Bergen's success on radio was paralleled in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") by [Peter Brough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brough "Peter Brough") and his dummy [Archie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews_(puppet) "Archie Andrews (puppet)") (_[Educating Archie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educating\_Archie "Educating Archie")_).

For the radio program, Bergen developed other characters, notably the slow-witted Mortimer Snerd and the man-hungry Effie Klinker. The star remained Charlie, who was always presented as a highly precocious child (albeit in [top hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_hat "Top hat"), cape, and [monocle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monocle "Monocle"))—a debonair, girl-crazy, child-about-town. As a child, and a wooden one at that, Charlie could get away with [double entendres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_entendres "Double entendres") which were otherwise impossible under broadcast standards of the time.

Bergen and Charlie with an NBC-produced comic book _On the Air_, 1947

Bergen was not a technically skilled ventriloquist, and Charlie McCarthy frequently twitted him for moving his lips. However, Bergen's sense of comedic timing was superb, and he handled Charlie's snappy dialog with aplomb. Bergen's wit in creating McCarthy's striking personality and that of his other characters was the making of the show. Bergen's popularity as a ventriloquist on radio, where the trick of "throwing his voice" was not visible, suggests his appeal was primarily the personality he applied to his characters.

Bergen and McCarthy are sometimes credited with "saving the world"[_[according to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] because, on the night of October 30, 1938, when [Orson Welles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orson_Welles "Orson Welles") performed his _[War of the Worlds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_War\_of\_the\_Worlds\_(radio) "The War of the Worlds (radio)")_ radio play that panicked many listeners, most of the American public had instead tuned to Bergen and McCarthy on another station and never heard Welles' play.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Conversely, it has also been theorized[_[according to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] that Bergen inadvertently contributed to the hysteria. When the musical portion of Bergen's show, _The Chase and Sanborn Hour_, aired approximately 12 minutes into the show, many listeners adjusted their dial and found the _War of the Worlds_ presentation already underway with a realistic-sounding reporter detailing terrible events.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Ray Noble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Noble_(musician) "Ray Noble (musician)") was the musical director and composer, and teenage singer [Anita Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Gordon "Anita Gordon") provided the songs on his show.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Gordon was said to have been discovered by Charlie, who had a crush on her.

In the fall (autumn) of 1948, Edgar and Charlie faced serious competition from [ABC's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Radio_Network "ABC Radio Network") "jackpot" quiz show, _[Stop the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop\_the\_Music\_(American\_TV\_series) "Stop the Music (American TV series)")_, which suddenly drew more listeners ([Fred Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Allen "Fred Allen") faced a similar problem because he directly appeared before them). In December 1948, Edgar announced he was temporarily "retiring" from radio, admitting that _Stop the Music_ was too popular to compete with.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] His final NBC broadcast was on December 26, 1948.

## _The Charlie McCarthy Show_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: The Charlie McCarthy Show")]

In October 1949, Bergen went to [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Radio_Network "CBS Radio Network"), with a new weekly program, _The Charlie McCarthy Show_, sponsored by [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-7) After their sponsorship ended in June 1952, [Warner-Hudnut, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner%E2%80%93Lambert "Warner–Lambert"), on behalf of "Lanolin Plus" cosmetics, primarily sponsored the series until the end of the 1953–54 season. In October 1954, [Kraft Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraft_Foods "Kraft Foods") sponsored a new _Edgar Bergen Hour_. After Kraft's departure, the series continued with participating sponsors as a 55-minute series in the fall of 1955. However, because more people were watching television on Sunday nights than listened to radio (and advertisers preferred to sponsor TV shows by then), the series finally ended on July 1, 1956.

## Comic strip

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Comic strip")]

In addition to his work as a ventriloquist, Bergen was also an actor and comic strip creator. He established the syndicated comic strip _Mortimer and Charlie_, which ran in newspapers from July 10, 1939, to May 1940,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-Holtz-8) illustrated first by [Ben Batsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Batsford "Ben Batsford")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-9) and then by Carl Buettner.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-10) The comic strip's writer was uncredited, but some of the gags certainly were lifted from the hit radio show.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-11) Between 1947 and 1954 [Harvey Eisenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Eisenberg "Harvey Eisenberg") also drew a comic strip based on Charlie McCarthy, scripted by Bergen.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-12)

Bergen in a [Vitaphone Varieties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitaphone_Varieties "Vitaphone Varieties") short, _Free and Easy_ (1931)

Bergen and his alter ego Charlie McCarthy were given top billing in several films, including the [Technicolor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technicolor "Technicolor") extravaganza _[The Goldwyn Follies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Goldwyn\_Follies "The Goldwyn Follies")_ (1938), opposite the [Ritz Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ritz_Brothers "Ritz Brothers"). That year they also appeared in _[You Can't Cheat an Honest Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Can't\_Cheat\_an\_Honest\_Man "You Can't Cheat an Honest Man")_ with [W. C. Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._C._Fields "W. C. Fields"). At the height of their popularity in 1937, Bergen was presented an [Honorary Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Honorary_Award "Academy Honorary Award") (in the form of a wooden Oscar statuette, the only wooden Oscar given so far) for his creation of Charlie McCarthy. Bergen, along with Charlie McCarthy and Mortimer Snerd, was also featured in the 1938 film _[Letter of Introduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letter\_of\_Introduction\_(film) "Letter of Introduction (film)")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

As an actor alone, Bergen portrayed the timid suitor of the sister Trina in _[I Remember Mama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Remember\_Mama\_(film) "I Remember Mama (film)")_ (1948), and appeared in _[Captain China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_China "Captain China")_ (1949), _[The Hanged Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hanged\_Man\_(1964\_film) "The Hanged Man (1964 film)")_ (1964) and _[Don't Make Waves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Make\_Waves "Don't Make Waves")_ (1967). Other film roles for the team include _[Look Who's Laughing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look\_Who's\_Laughing "Look Who's Laughing")_ (1941) and _[Here We Go Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_Again\_(film) "Here We Go Again (film)")_ (1942), both with [Fibber McGee and Molly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibber_McGee_and_Molly "Fibber McGee and Molly"). Charlie McCarthy wore a US Army uniform in _[Stage Door Canteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stage\_Door\_Canteen\_(film) "Stage Door Canteen (film)")_ (1943) with Mortimer Snerd. Bergen, McCarthy and Snerd were also featured in [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney")'s _[Fun and Fancy Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fun\_and\_Fancy\_Free "Fun and Fancy Free")_ (1947). He later cameoed in all-star films such as _[The Phynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phynx "The Phynx")_ (1970), _[Won Ton Ton, the Dog Who Saved Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Won\_Ton\_Ton,\_the\_Dog\_Who\_Saved\_Hollywood "Won Ton Ton, the Dog Who Saved Hollywood")_ (1976), and _[The Muppet Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Movie "The Muppet Movie")_ (1979). In 1977, Bergen had made a guest appearance on a second-season episode of _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_, the highly acclaimed television comedy/variety program produced by [Jim Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson") who considered Bergen a major inspiration.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-13) His daughter Candice had also guest-starred on the show during its first season. Bergen died shortly after filming his _Muppet Movie_ scene, which was also his final public appearance, and was subsequently dedicated to him. In 2009 Bergen was featured in the comedy documentary _[I'm No Dummy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_No\_Dummy "I'm No Dummy")_,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-14) directed by [Bryan W. Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_W._Simon "Bryan W. Simon").
