Although his regular series never made the transition to [television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television "Television"), Bergen made numerous appearances on the medium during his career. His first appearance was with Charlie McCarthy on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")'s pioneering television variety show _[Hour Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour\_Glass\_(TV\_series) "Hour Glass (TV series)")_ in November 1946. In a filmed [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving "Thanksgiving") special, billed as his official TV debut, sponsored by [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola") on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") in 1950, the new character Podine Puffington was introduced; this saucy Southern belle was as tall as a real woman, in contrast to Bergen's other sit-on-the-knee sized characters. On Christmas Day that same year, Bergen and McCarthy appeared as guests on [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney")'s first television show, _[One Hour in Wonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Hour\_in\_Wonderland "One Hour in Wonderland")_.

In 1954, Bergen was a co-host on a memorable TV musical special, _[General Foods 25th Anniversary Show: A Salute to Rodgers and Hammerstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General\_Foods\_25th\_Anniversary\_Show:\_A\_Salute\_to\_Rodgers\_and\_Hammerstein "General Foods 25th Anniversary Show: A Salute to Rodgers and Hammerstein")_.

On December 26, 1954, Bergen appeared on _[What's My Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's\_My\_Line "What's My Line")_ as a mystery guest. Bergen also hosted the television game show _[Do You Trust Your Wife?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Do\_You\_Trust%3F "Who Do You Trust?")_ in 1956–1957, later succeeded, in a daytime edition, by [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson").

He appeared in the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas "Christmas") 1957 episode of [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Broadcasting_Company "National Broadcasting Company")'s _[The Gisele MacKenzie Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gisele\_MacKenzie\_Show "The Gisele MacKenzie Show")_. In 1958, Bergen appeared with his 12-year-old daughter [Candice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen") on an episode of _[You Bet Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Bet\_Your\_Life "You Bet Your Life")_ starring [Groucho Marx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groucho_Marx "Groucho Marx"). In 1959, he appeared in the second episode titled "Dossier" of the NBC [espionage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espionage "Espionage")[series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_series "Television series")_[Five Fingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_Fingers\_(American\_TV\_series) "Five Fingers (American TV series)")_ starring [David Hedison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hedison "David Hedison"). On May 21, 1959, he guest-starred with Charlie McCarthy on NBC's _[The Ford Show, Starring Tennessee Ernie Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ford\_Show "The Ford Show")_. Bergen continued to appear regularly on television during the 1960s and into the 1970s, appearing on _[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_ as late as 1977. He guest-starred as Charlie in the 1960 episode "Moment of Fear" of [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Broadcasting_System "Columbia Broadcasting System")'s _[The DuPont Show with June Allyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_DuPont\_Show\_with\_June\_Allyson "The DuPont Show with June Allyson")_. He did a stint as one of the _[What's My Line?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's\_My\_Line%3F "What's My Line?")_ mystery guests on the popular Sunday night CBS series. His colleague [Paul Winchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Winchell "Paul Winchell") happened to be a panel member during that episode.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-15) Bergen appeared on the NBC interview program _[Here's Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here's\_Hollywood "Here's Hollywood")_.

Bergen appeared as Grandpa Zeb Walton in the original _[Waltons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Waltons "The Waltons")_ television movie, _[The Homecoming: A Christmas Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Homecoming:\_A\_Christmas\_Story "The Homecoming: A Christmas Story")_ (1971). The role was played by [Will Geer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Geer "Will Geer") in the subsequent TV series. During the run of _The Waltons_—which took place throughout the 1930s and 1940s—the voices of Bergen and Charlie McCarthy were sporadically heard from the Waltons' radio, as family members regularly tuned in for that program.

He appeared on _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ in Season 2. His daughter, [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen") had appeared in Season 1.

## Family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Family")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Yancy_Derringer_cast_2.JPG/250px-Yancy_Derringer_cast_2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yancy_Derringer_cast_2.JPG)

[X Brands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Brands "X Brands"), [Frances Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Bergen "Frances Bergen"), and [Jock Mahoney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jock_Mahoney "Jock Mahoney") in _[Yancy Derringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yancy\_Derringer "Yancy Derringer")_ (1959)

In 1941, Bergen met 18-year-old [Frances Westerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Bergen "Frances Bergen"), a young fashion model who had graduated from Los Angeles High School the prior year. He spotted her in the audience of his radio program, where she was the guest of one of his staff members. A long-distance courtship, spanning years, ensued. The two were married in Mexico on June 28, 1945.

On May 9, 1946, Frances gave birth to future actress [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen"), whose first performances were on Bergen's radio show. By 1950, the family lived on Beverly Grove Drive in Los Angeles.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-16) The couple's second child was film and TV editor Kris Bergen. Frances also acted in several movies, co-starred in the 1958 TV series _[Yancy Derringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yancy\_Derringer "Yancy Derringer")_, and guest-starred in many other shows.

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Death")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Candice_Bergen.jpg/250px-Candice_Bergen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Candice_Bergen.jpg)

Bergen's daughter Candice Bergen and his wife, actress [Frances Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Bergen "Frances Bergen"), at the 62nd Academy Awards in 1990

In mid-September 1978, Bergen announced his retirement and sent his monocled, top-hatted partner, Charlie McCarthy, to the [National Museum of American History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_American_History "National Museum of American History") at the [Smithsonian Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Institution "Smithsonian Institution") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") He opened for Andy Williams at [Caesar's Palace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesar's_Palace_Hotel "Caesar's Palace Hotel") Las Vegas on September 27, for a two-week "Farewell to Show Business" engagement. Three days later, on September 30, 1978, he died of kidney disease.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-17) Bergen was interred with his parents (buried under their true surname of "Berggren") in [Inglewood Park Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood_Park_Cemetery "Inglewood Park Cemetery"), [Inglewood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California").

In his will, according to Candice Bergen's memoir, _A Fine Romance_, he left his daughter nothing but bequeathed his dummy, Charlie McCarthy, $10,000. "I'd chased my father's approval all my life, and here was proof I'd never get it," the actress wrote. "I was hurt, shocked, when I discovered he had left me out of his will." She further explained that her father had provided this inheritance for the dummy so that the funds could be managed, invested, and reinvested to provide for his future performances. She said her father wrote in his will: "I make this provision for sentimental reasons, which to me are vital due to the association with Charlie McCarthy, who has been my constant companion and who has taken on the character of a real person and from whom I have never been separated even for a day." Throughout the book, she suggested that her father seemed to have a stronger kinship with Charlie than with her. The dummy "dominated" her childhood, she explained, and even had his own bedroom in their house. "Those were unique circumstances to grow up in," she wrote. "Sometimes I have to give myself credit for being a functional human being. I knew my father loved me, but with his Swedish reserve, it wasn't his nature to tell me."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-18)

A message in the [closing credits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closing_credits "Closing credits") dedicates _[The Muppet Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Movie "The Muppet Movie")_ (which featured Bergen and Charlie in their last screen appearance) to the memory and magic of Bergen. In 1990, Bergen was elected to the [Radio Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Hall_of_Fame "Radio Hall of Fame"), the same year that _The Charlie McCarthy Show_ was selected as an honored program. In 1991, the United States Postal Service honored him with a 29-cent commemorative stamp.

On October 2, 2006, Bergen's widow, Frances Westerman Bergen, died at [Cedars-Sinai Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedars-Sinai_Medical_Center "Cedars-Sinai Medical Center") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), aged 84, from undisclosed causes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-19) Unlike her husband, she is buried in [Forest Lawn Memorial Park (Hollywood Hills)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Lawn_Memorial_Park_(Hollywood_Hills) "Forest Lawn Memorial Park (Hollywood Hills)").

## Hollywood Walk of Fame

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Hollywood Walk of Fame")]

Bergen was inducted into the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") with three stars in 1960, for his contributions to television, [motion pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_actors_with_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame_motion_picture_stars "List of actors with Hollywood Walk of Fame motion picture stars"), and radio. The stars are located at 6425, 6766, and 6801 [Hollywood Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard"), respectively.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-20)

**Edgar John Bergen** (né **Berggren**; February 16, 1903– September 30, 1978) was an American ventriloquist, comedian, actor, vaudevillian and radio performer. He was best known for his characters [Charlie McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_McCarthy "Charlie McCarthy") and Mortimer Snerd. Bergen pioneered modern-day [ventriloquism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventriloquism "Ventriloquism") and has been described by puppetry organization [UNIMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNIMA "UNIMA") as the “quintessential ventriloquist of the 20th century”.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-1) He was the father of actress [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Edgar_Bergen_and_Charlie_McCarthy_1926.jpg/250px-Edgar_Bergen_and_Charlie_McCarthy_1926.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Edgar_Bergen_and_Charlie_McCarthy_1926.jpg)

Bergen and [Charlie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_McCarthy_(ventriloquist) "Charlie McCarthy (ventriloquist)") in 1926

Bergen was born in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), one of five children and the younger of two sons of [Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden") immigrants Nilla Svensdotter (née Osberg) and Johan Henriksson Berggren.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-2) He lived on a farm near [Decatur, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decatur,_Michigan "Decatur, Michigan") until he was four, when his family returned to Sweden, where he learned the language. After his family had returned to Chicago, when he was eleven, he taught himself ventriloquism from a pamphlet called "The Wizard's Manual". He attended [Lake View High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_View_High_School_(Chicago,_Illinois) "Lake View High School (Chicago, Illinois)"). After his father died, when Edgar was 16, he went out to work as an apprentice accountant, a furnace stoker, a player-piano operator, and a projectionist in a silent-movie house.

Edgar so impressed the famous ventriloquist [Harry Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Lester_(ventriloquist) "Harry Lester (ventriloquist)") that he gave the teenager almost daily lessons for three months in the fundamentals of ventriloquism. In the fall of 1919, Edgar paid Chicago woodcarver Theodore Mack $36 ($688.59 in 2025) to sculpt a likeness of a rascally red-headed Irish [newspaper boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper_hawker "Newspaper hawker") he knew. The head went on a [dummy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventriloquism "Ventriloquism") named Charlie McCarthy, which became Bergen's lifelong [sidekick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidekick "Sidekick"). He had created the body himself, using a nine-inch length of broomstick for the backbone, and rubber bands and cords to control the lower jaw mechanism of the mouth.

For college, he attended [Northwestern University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University "Northwestern University"), where he enrolled in the pre-med program to please his mother. He later switched to speech and drama, but never completed his degree.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-3) He gave his first public performance at Waveland Avenue Congregational Church located on the northeast corner of Waveland and Janssen. He lived across the street from the church. In 1965, he gave the church a generous contribution, a thoughtful letter, and a photograph of himself which had been requested by the minister and was displayed in the church's assembly room which was dedicated to Bergen. He cut out an "R" and a "G" from his family name and went from Berggren to Bergen on the showbills. Between June 1922 and August 1925, he performed every summer on the professional [Chautauqua circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chautauqua_circuit "Chautauqua circuit") and at the Lyceum theater in Chicago. Bergen had an interest in aviation, becoming a private pilot.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-4)

## _The Chase and Sanborn Hour_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: The Chase and Sanborn Hour")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Chase_and_Sanborn_Hour.jpg/250px-Chase_and_Sanborn_Hour.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chase_and_Sanborn_Hour.jpg)

Edgar Bergen and his dummy Charlie McCarthy with [W. C. Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._C._Fields "W. C. Fields") on _[The Chase and Sanborn Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_and\_Sanborn\_Hour "The Chase and Sanborn Hour")_

His first performances were in [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville"), at which point he legally changed his last name to the easier-to-pronounce "Bergen". He worked in one-reel [movie shorts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_subject "Short subject"), but his real success was on the radio. He and Charlie were seen at a New York party by [Elsa Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa_Maxwell "Elsa Maxwell") for [Noël Coward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No%C3%ABl_Coward "Noël Coward"), who recommended them for an engagement at the famous [Rainbow Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Room "Rainbow Room"). It was there that two producers saw Bergen and Charlie perform. They then recommended them for a guest appearance on [Rudy Vallée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Vall%C3%A9e "Rudy Vallée")'s program.

Their initial appearance (December 17, 1936) was so successful that the following year they were given regular cast roles as part of _[The Chase and Sanborn Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_and\_Sanborn\_Hour "The Chase and Sanborn Hour")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-Dunning-5) Under various sponsors (and two different networks), they were on the air from May 9, 1937, to July 1, 1956. The popularity of a ventriloquist on radio, when one could see neither the dummies nor his skill, surprised and puzzled many critics, then and now. Even knowing that Bergen provided the voice, listeners perceived Charlie as a genuine person.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-6) In 1947, Sam Berman caricatured Bergen and McCarthy for the network's glossy promotional book, _NBC Parade of Stars: As Heard Over Your Favorite NBC Station_.

Bergen's skill as an entertainer, especially his characterization of Charlie, carried the show (many recordings of which have survived).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-Dunning-5) Bergen's success on radio was paralleled in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") by [Peter Brough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brough "Peter Brough") and his dummy [Archie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews_(puppet) "Archie Andrews (puppet)") (_[Educating Archie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educating\_Archie "Educating Archie")_).

For the radio program, Bergen developed other characters, notably the slow-witted Mortimer Snerd and the man-hungry Effie Klinker. The star remained Charlie, who was always presented as a highly precocious child (albeit in [top hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_hat "Top hat"), cape, and [monocle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monocle "Monocle"))—a debonair, girl-crazy, child-about-town. As a child, and a wooden one at that, Charlie could get away with [double entendres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_entendres "Double entendres") which were otherwise impossible under broadcast standards of the time.

**Charlie:** "May I have a kiss good-bye?"**[Dale Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Evans "Dale Evans"):** "Well, I can't see any harm in that!"**Charlie:** "Oh. I wish you could. A harmless kiss doesn't sound very thrilling."
Charlie and [Mae West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mae_West "Mae West") had this conversation in 1937.

**Charlie:** "Not so loud, Mae, not so loud! All my girlfriends are listening."**Mae:** "Oh, yeah! You're all wood and a yard long."**Charlie:** "Yeah."**Mae:** "You weren't so nervous and backward when you came up to see me at my apartment. In fact, you didn't need any encouragement to kiss me."**Charlie:** "Did I do that?"**Mae:** "Why, you certainly did. I got marks to prove it. An' splinters, too."
Charlie's feud with [W. C. Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._C._Fields "W. C. Fields") was a regular feature of the show.

**W. C. Fields:** "Well, if it isn't Charlie McCarthy, the woodpecker's pinup boy!"**Charlie:** "Well, if it isn't W.C. Fields, the man who keeps Seagram's in business!"**W. C. You may come unglued."**Charlie:** "Mind if I stand in the shade of your nose?"[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Edgar_Bergen_Charlie_McCarthy_1947.JPG/250px-Edgar_Bergen_Charlie_McCarthy_1947.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Edgar_Bergen_Charlie_McCarthy_1947.JPG)

Bergen and Charlie with an NBC-produced comic book _On the Air_, 1947

Bergen was not a technically skilled ventriloquist, and Charlie McCarthy frequently twitted him for moving his lips. However, Bergen's sense of comedic timing was superb, and he handled Charlie's snappy dialog with aplomb. Bergen's wit in creating McCarthy's striking personality and that of his other characters was the making of the show. Bergen's popularity as a ventriloquist on radio, where the trick of "throwing his voice" was not visible, suggests his appeal was primarily the personality he applied to his characters.

Bergen and McCarthy are sometimes credited with "saving the world"[_[according to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] because, on the night of October 30, 1938, when [Orson Welles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orson_Welles "Orson Welles") performed his _[War of the Worlds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_War\_of\_the\_Worlds\_(radio) "The War of the Worlds (radio)")_ radio play that panicked many listeners, most of the American public had instead tuned to Bergen and McCarthy on another station and never heard Welles' play.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Conversely, it has also been theorized[_[according to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] that Bergen inadvertently contributed to the hysteria. When the musical portion of Bergen's show, _The Chase and Sanborn Hour_, aired approximately 12 minutes into the show, many listeners adjusted their dial and found the _War of the Worlds_ presentation already underway with a realistic-sounding reporter detailing terrible events.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Ray Noble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Noble_(musician) "Ray Noble (musician)") was the musical director and composer, and teenage singer [Anita Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Gordon "Anita Gordon") provided the songs on his show.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Gordon was said to have been discovered by Charlie, who had a crush on her.

In the fall (autumn) of 1948, Edgar and Charlie faced serious competition from [ABC's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Radio_Network "ABC Radio Network") "jackpot" quiz show, _[Stop the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop\_the\_Music\_(American\_TV\_series) "Stop the Music (American TV series)")_, which suddenly drew more listeners ([Fred Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Allen "Fred Allen") faced a similar problem because he directly appeared before them). In December 1948, Edgar announced he was temporarily "retiring" from radio, admitting that _Stop the Music_ was too popular to compete with.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] His final NBC broadcast was on December 26, 1948.

## _The Charlie McCarthy Show_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: The Charlie McCarthy Show")]

In October 1949, Bergen went to [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Radio_Network "CBS Radio Network"), with a new weekly program, _The Charlie McCarthy Show_, sponsored by [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-7) After their sponsorship ended in June 1952, [Warner-Hudnut, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner%E2%80%93Lambert "Warner–Lambert"), on behalf of "Lanolin Plus" cosmetics, primarily sponsored the series until the end of the 1953–54 season. In October 1954, [Kraft Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraft_Foods "Kraft Foods") sponsored a new _Edgar Bergen Hour_. After Kraft's departure, the series continued with participating sponsors as a 55-minute series in the fall of 1955. However, because more people were watching television on Sunday nights than listened to radio (and advertisers preferred to sponsor TV shows by then), the series finally ended on July 1, 1956.

## Comic strip

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Comic strip")]

In addition to his work as a ventriloquist, Bergen was also an actor and comic strip creator. He established the syndicated comic strip _Mortimer and Charlie_, which ran in newspapers from July 10, 1939, to May 1940,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-Holtz-8) illustrated first by [Ben Batsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Batsford "Ben Batsford")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-9) and then by Carl Buettner.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-10) The comic strip's writer was uncredited, but some of the gags certainly were lifted from the hit radio show.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-11) Between 1947 and 1954 [Harvey Eisenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Eisenberg "Harvey Eisenberg") also drew a comic strip based on Charlie McCarthy, scripted by Bergen.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-12)

Charlie McCarthy wore a US Army uniform in _[Stage Door Canteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stage\_Door\_Canteen\_(film) "Stage Door Canteen (film)")_ (1943) with Mortimer Snerd. Bergen, McCarthy and Snerd were also featured in [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney")'s _[Fun and Fancy Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fun\_and\_Fancy\_Free "Fun and Fancy Free")_ (1947). He later cameoed in all-star films such as _[The Phynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phynx "The Phynx")_ (1970), _[Won Ton Ton, the Dog Who Saved Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Won\_Ton\_Ton,\_the\_Dog\_Who\_Saved\_Hollywood "Won Ton Ton, the Dog Who Saved Hollywood")_ (1976), and _[The Muppet Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Movie "The Muppet Movie")_ (1979). In 1977, Bergen had made a guest appearance on a second-season episode of _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_, the highly acclaimed television comedy/variety program produced by [Jim Henson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson") who considered Bergen a major inspiration.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-13) His daughter Candice had also guest-starred on the show during its first season. Bergen died shortly after filming his _Muppet Movie_ scene, which was also his final public appearance, and was subsequently dedicated to him. In 2009 Bergen was featured in the comedy documentary _[I'm No Dummy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_No\_Dummy "I'm No Dummy")_,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-14) directed by [Bryan W. Although his regular series never made the transition to [television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television "Television"), Bergen made numerous appearances on the medium during his career. His first appearance was with Charlie McCarthy on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")'s pioneering television variety show _[Hour Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour\_Glass\_(TV\_series) "Hour Glass (TV series)")_ in November 1946. In a filmed [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving "Thanksgiving") special, billed as his official TV debut, sponsored by [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola") on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") in 1950, the new character Podine Puffington was introduced; this saucy Southern belle was as tall as a real woman, in contrast to Bergen's other sit-on-the-knee sized characters. On Christmas Day that same year, Bergen and McCarthy appeared as guests on [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney")'s first television show, _[One Hour in Wonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Hour\_in\_Wonderland "One Hour in Wonderland")_.

In 1954, Bergen was a co-host on a memorable TV musical special, _[General Foods 25th Anniversary Show: A Salute to Rodgers and Hammerstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General\_Foods\_25th\_Anniversary\_Show:\_A\_Salute\_to\_Rodgers\_and\_Hammerstein "General Foods 25th Anniversary Show: A Salute to Rodgers and Hammerstein")_.

On December 26, 1954, Bergen appeared on _[What's My Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's\_My\_Line "What's My Line")_ as a mystery guest. Bergen also hosted the television game show _[Do You Trust Your Wife?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Do\_You\_Trust%3F "Who Do You Trust?")_ in 1956–1957, later succeeded, in a daytime edition, by [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson").

He appeared in the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas "Christmas") 1957 episode of [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Broadcasting_Company "National Broadcasting Company")'s _[The Gisele MacKenzie Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gisele\_MacKenzie\_Show "The Gisele MacKenzie Show")_. In 1958, Bergen appeared with his 12-year-old daughter [Candice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen") on an episode of _[You Bet Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Bet\_Your\_Life "You Bet Your Life")_ starring [Groucho Marx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groucho_Marx "Groucho Marx"). In 1959, he appeared in the second episode titled "Dossier" of the NBC [espionage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espionage "Espionage")[series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_series "Television series")_[Five Fingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_Fingers\_(American\_TV\_series) "Five Fingers (American TV series)")_ starring [David Hedison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hedison "David Hedison"). On May 21, 1959, he guest-starred with Charlie McCarthy on NBC's _[The Ford Show, Starring Tennessee Ernie Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ford\_Show "The Ford Show")_. Bergen continued to appear regularly on television during the 1960s and into the 1970s, appearing on _[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_ as late as 1977. He guest-starred as Charlie in the 1960 episode "Moment of Fear" of [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Broadcasting_System "Columbia Broadcasting System")'s _[The DuPont Show with June Allyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_DuPont\_Show\_with\_June\_Allyson "The DuPont Show with June Allyson")_. He did a stint as one of the _[What's My Line?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's\_My\_Line%3F "What's My Line?")_ mystery guests on the popular Sunday night CBS series. His colleague [Paul Winchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Winchell "Paul Winchell") happened to be a panel member during that episode.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-15) Bergen appeared on the NBC interview program _[Here's Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here's\_Hollywood "Here's Hollywood")_.

Bergen appeared as Grandpa Zeb Walton in the original _[Waltons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Waltons "The Waltons")_ television movie, _[The Homecoming: A Christmas Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Homecoming:\_A\_Christmas\_Story "The Homecoming: A Christmas Story")_ (1971). The role was played by [Will Geer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Geer "Will Geer") in the subsequent TV series. During the run of _The Waltons_—which took place throughout the 1930s and 1940s—the voices of Bergen and Charlie McCarthy were sporadically heard from the Waltons' radio, as family members regularly tuned in for that program.

He appeared on _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ in Season 2. His daughter, [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen") had appeared in Season 1.

## Family

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Yancy_Derringer_cast_2.JPG/250px-Yancy_Derringer_cast_2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yancy_Derringer_cast_2.JPG)

[X Brands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Brands "X Brands"), [Frances Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Bergen "Frances Bergen"), and [Jock Mahoney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jock_Mahoney "Jock Mahoney") in _[Yancy Derringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yancy\_Derringer "Yancy Derringer")_ (1959)

In 1941, Bergen met 18-year-old [Frances Westerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Bergen "Frances Bergen"), a young fashion model who had graduated from Los Angeles High School the prior year. He spotted her in the audience of his radio program, where she was the guest of one of his staff members. A long-distance courtship, spanning years, ensued. The two were married in Mexico on June 28, 1945.

On May 9, 1946, Frances gave birth to future actress [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen"), whose first performances were on Bergen's radio show. By 1950, the family lived on Beverly Grove Drive in Los Angeles.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-16) The couple's second child was film and TV editor Kris Bergen. Frances also acted in several movies, co-starred in the 1958 TV series _[Yancy Derringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yancy\_Derringer "Yancy Derringer")_, and guest-starred in many other shows.

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Death")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Candice_Bergen.jpg/250px-Candice_Bergen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Candice_Bergen.jpg)

Bergen's daughter Candice Bergen and his wife, actress [Frances Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Bergen "Frances Bergen"), at the 62nd Academy Awards in 1990

In mid-September 1978, Bergen announced his retirement and sent his monocled, top-hatted partner, Charlie McCarthy, to the [National Museum of American History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_American_History "National Museum of American History") at the [Smithsonian Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Institution "Smithsonian Institution") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") He opened for Andy Williams at [Caesar's Palace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesar's_Palace_Hotel "Caesar's Palace Hotel") Las Vegas on September 27, for a two-week "Farewell to Show Business" engagement. Three days later, on September 30, 1978, he died of kidney disease.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-17) Bergen was interred with his parents (buried under their true surname of "Berggren") in [Inglewood Park Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood_Park_Cemetery "Inglewood Park Cemetery"), [Inglewood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California").

In his will, according to Candice Bergen's memoir, _A Fine Romance_, he left his daughter nothing but bequeathed his dummy, Charlie McCarthy, $10,000. "I'd chased my father's approval all my life, and here was proof I'd never get it," the actress wrote. "I was hurt, shocked, when I discovered he had left me out of his will." She further explained that her father had provided this inheritance for the dummy so that the funds could be managed, invested, and reinvested to provide for his future performances. She said her father wrote in his will: "I make this provision for sentimental reasons, which to me are vital due to the association with Charlie McCarthy, who has been my constant companion and who has taken on the character of a real person and from whom I have never been separated even for a day." Throughout the book, she suggested that her father seemed to have a stronger kinship with Charlie than with her. The dummy "dominated" her childhood, she explained, and even had his own bedroom in their house. "Those were unique circumstances to grow up in," she wrote. "Sometimes I have to give myself credit for being a functional human being. I knew my father loved me, but with his Swedish reserve, it wasn't his nature to tell me."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-18)

A message in the [closing credits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closing_credits "Closing credits") dedicates _[The Muppet Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Movie "The Muppet Movie")_ (which featured Bergen and Charlie in their last screen appearance) to the memory and magic of Bergen. In 1990, Bergen was elected to the [Radio Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Hall_of_Fame "Radio Hall of Fame"), the same year that _The Charlie McCarthy Show_ was selected as an honored program. In 1991, the United States Postal Service honored him with a 29-cent commemorative stamp.

On October 2, 2006, Bergen's widow, Frances Westerman Bergen, died at [Cedars-Sinai Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedars-Sinai_Medical_Center "Cedars-Sinai Medical Center") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), aged 84, from undisclosed causes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-19) Unlike her husband, she is buried in [Forest Lawn Memorial Park (Hollywood Hills)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Lawn_Memorial_Park_(Hollywood_Hills) "Forest Lawn Memorial Park (Hollywood Hills)").

## Hollywood Walk of Fame

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edgar_Bergen&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Hollywood Walk of Fame")]

Bergen was inducted into the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") with three stars in 1960, for his contributions to television, [motion pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_actors_with_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame_motion_picture_stars "List of actors with Hollywood Walk of Fame motion picture stars"), and radio. The stars are located at 6425, 6766, and 6801 [Hollywood Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard"), respectively.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bergen#cite_note-20)
